tasyābhidhyāyataścaiva tiryaksrotā hyavartata
tasmāt tiryakpravṛttaḥ sa tiryaksrotās tataḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.70.d:
तस्याभिध्यायतश्चैव तिर्यक्स्रोता ह्यवर्तत
तस्मात् तिर्यक्प्रवृत्तः स तिर्यक्स्रोतास् ततः स्मृतः ॥
1.70.m: As he meditated, the transverse-current [creation] (tiryaksrotas) arose. / Because it proceeded horizontally (tiryak), it is known as the transverse-current creation.

1.70.s:
paśvādayaste vikhyātā utpathagrāhiṇo dvijāḥ
tasyābhidhyāyato 'nyaṃ vai sāttvikaḥ samavartata //
1.70.d:
पश्वादयस्ते विख्याता उत्पथग्राहिणो द्विजाः
तस्याभिध्यायतो ऽन्यं वै सात्त्विकः समवर्तत ॥
1.70.m: They are known as beasts and the like, taking the wrong path, O twice-born. / As he meditated upon another, a sāttvika [creation] arose.

1.70.s:
ūrdhvasrotāstṛtīyastu sa vai cordhvaṃ vyavasthitaḥ
yasmātpravartate cordhvam ūrdhvasrotāstataḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.70.d:
ऊर्ध्वस्रोतास्तृतीयस्तु स वै चोर्ध्वं व्यवस्थितः
यस्मात्प्रवर्तते चोर्ध्वम् ऊर्ध्वस्रोतास्ततः स्मृतः ॥
1.70.m: The third is the upward-current [creation] (ūrdhvasrotas), situated above. / Because it proceeds upward, it is known as the upward-current creation.

1.70.s:
te sukhaprītibahulā bahirantaś ca saṃvṛtāḥ
prakāśā bahirantaś ca ūrdhvasrotobhavāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
ते सुखप्रीतिबहुला बहिरन्तश् च संवृताः
प्रकाशा बहिरन्तश् च ऊर्ध्वस्रोतोभवाः स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: Full of joy and pleasure, enveloped outside and inside, / luminous outside and inside, they are known as beings born of the upward current.

1.70.s:
te sattvasya ca yogena sṛṣṭāḥ sattvodbhavāḥ smṛtāḥ
ūrdhvasrotāstṛtīyo vai devasargastu sa smṛtaḥ //
1.70.d:
ते सत्त्वस्य च योगेन सृष्टाः सत्त्वोद्भवाः स्मृताः
ऊर्ध्वस्रोतास्तृतीयो वै देवसर्गस्तु स स्मृतः ॥
1.70.m: Created through the union with sattva, they are known as arisen from sattva. / The third is indeed the upward-current, known as the creation of the gods.

1.70.s:
prakāśād bahirantaś ca ūrdhvasrotodbhavāḥ smṛtāḥ
te ūrdhvasrotaso jñeyās tuṣṭātmāno budhaiḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
प्रकाशाद् बहिरन्तश् च ऊर्ध्वस्रोतोद्भवाः स्मृताः
ते ऊर्ध्वस्रोतसो ज्ञेयास् तुष्टात्मानो बुधैः स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: Because of illumination outside and inside, they are known as born of the upward current; / they are to be understood as upward-current beings, remembered by the wise as contented in nature.

1.70.s:
ūrdhvasrotaḥsu sṛṣṭeṣu deveṣu varadaḥ prabhuḥ
prītimānabhavadbrahmā tato 'nyaṃ so 'bhyamanyata //
1.70.d:
ऊर्ध्वस्रोतःसु सृष्टेषु देवेषु वरदः प्रभुः
प्रीतिमानभवद्ब्रह्मा ततो ऽन्यं सो ऽभ्यमन्यत ॥
1.70.m: When the upward-current gods had been created, the boon-giving lord / Brahmā was pleased; then he considered another [creation].

1.70.s:
sasarja sargamanyaṃ hi sādhakaṃ prabhurīśvaraḥ
tato 'bhidhyāyatastasya satyābhidhyāyinastadā //
1.70.d:
ससर्ज सर्गमन्यं हि साधकं प्रभुरीश्वरः
ततो ऽभिध्यायतस्तस्य सत्याभिध्यायिनस्तदा ॥
1.70.m: The sovereign lord created another creation, one capable of accomplishing ends. / Then, as he who meditates on truth was meditating,

1.70.s:
prādurāsīttadā vyaktād arvāksrotāstu sādhakaḥ
yasmād arvāṅnyavartanta tato 'rvāksrotasas tu te //
1.70.d:
प्रादुरासीत्तदा व्यक्ताद् अर्वाक्स्रोतास्तु साधकः
यस्माद् अर्वाङ्न्यवर्तन्त ततो ऽर्वाक्स्रोतसस् तु ते ॥
1.70.m: there arose from the unmanifest the downward-current [creation] (arvāksrotas), the effective agent. / Because they proceeded downwards, they are called the downward-current beings.

1.70.s:
te ca prakāśabahulās tamaḥpṛktā rajo 'dhikāḥ
tasmātte duḥkhabahulā bhūyobhūyaś ca kāriṇaḥ //
1.70.d:
ते च प्रकाशबहुलास् तमःपृक्ता रजो ऽधिकाः
तस्मात्ते दुःखबहुला भूयोभूयश् च कारिणः ॥
1.70.m: They abound in light, are mixed with tamas, and have an excess of rajas. / Therefore they abound in sorrow and act again and again.

1.70.s: saṃvṛtā bahirantaś ca manuṣyāḥ sādhakāś ca te //
1.70.d: संवृता बहिरन्तश् च मनुष्याः साधकाश् च ते ॥
1.70.m: Enveloped outside and inside, they are human beings, the effective agents.

1.70.s: lakṣaṇaistārakādyaiste hy aṣṭadhā tu vyavasthitāḥ //
1.70.d: लक्षणैस्तारकाद्यैस्ते ह्य् अष्टधा तु व्यवस्थिताः ॥
1.70.m: Through characteristics beginning with tāraka, they are arranged into eight kinds.

1.70.s:
siddhātmāno manuṣyāste gandharvasahadharmiṇaḥ
ityeṣa taijasaḥ sargo hy arvāksrotaḥprakīrtitaḥ //
1.70.d:
सिद्धात्मानो मनुष्यास्ते गन्धर्वसहधर्मिणः
इत्येष तैजसः सर्गो ह्य् अर्वाक्स्रोतःप्रकीर्तितः ॥
1.70.m: Those human beings are accomplished souls, sharing the nature of the Gandharvas. / Thus this radiant creation is proclaimed as the downward-current creation.

1.70.s:
pañcamo 'nugrahaḥ sargaś caturdhā tu vyavasthitaḥ
viparyayeṇa śaktyā ca siddhyā tuṣṭyā tathaiva ca //
1.70.d:
पञ्चमो ऽनुग्रहः सर्गश् चतुर्धा तु व्यवस्थितः
विपर्ययेण शक्त्या च सिद्ध्या तुष्ट्या तथैव च ॥
1.70.m: The fifth is the creation of grace (anugraha), arranged in four ways: / by inversion (viparyaya), incapacity (aśakti), perfection (siddhi), and contentment (tuṣṭi).

1.70.s:
sthāvareṣu viparyāsas tiryagyoniṣu śaktitaḥ
siddhātmāno manuṣyāstu ṛṣideveṣu kṛtsnaśaḥ //
1.70.d:
स्थावरेषु विपर्यासस् तिर्यग्योनिषु शक्तितः
सिद्धात्मानो मनुष्यास्तु ऋषिदेवेषु कृत्स्नशः ॥
1.70.m: Inversion is in immovable beings, incapacity in animal wombs; / perfected souls are in human beings, and completely so among sages and gods.

1.70.s:
ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargo vaikṛto navamaḥ smṛtaḥ
bhūtādikānāṃ bhūtānāṃ ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ sa ucyate //
1.70.d:
इत्येष प्राकृतः सर्गो वैकृतो नवमः स्मृतः
भूतादिकानां भूतानां षष्ठः सर्गः स उच्यते ॥
1.70.m: This is the primary creation; the secondary creation is known as the ninth. / The creation of beings beginning with the bhūtas is called the sixth.

1.70.s:
nivṛttaṃ vartamānaṃ ca teṣāṃ jānanti vai punaḥ
bhūtādikānāṃ bhūtānāṃ saptamaḥ sarga eva ca //
1.70.d:
निवृत्तं वर्तमानं च तेषां जानन्ति वै पुनः
भूतादिकानां भूतानां सप्तमः सर्ग एव च ॥
1.70.m: Moreover, they know what has passed and what is present. / The creation of beings beginning with the bhūtas is also the seventh.

1.70.s:
te parigrāhiṇaḥ sarve saṃvibhāgaratāḥ punaḥ
svādanāś cāpyaśīlāś ca jñeyā bhūtādikāś ca te //
1.70.d:
ते परिग्राहिणः सर्वे संविभागरताः पुनः
स्वादनाश् चाप्यशीलाश् च ज्ञेया भूतादिकाश् च ते ॥
1.70.m: They are all possessive, yet delighting in sharing; / they are relishers, yet devoid of good conduct; they are to be known as beings beginning with the bhūtas.

1.70.s:
viparyayeṇa bhūtādir aśaktyā ca vyavasthitaḥ
prathamo mahataḥ sargo vijñeyo brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.70.d:
विपर्ययेण भूतादिर् अशक्त्या च व्यवस्थितः
प्रथमो महतः सर्गो विज्ञेयो ब्रह्मणः स्मृतः ॥
1.70.m: The category beginning with the bhūtas is established through inversion and incapacity. / The first creation of Brahmā is to be understood as that of the Mahat.

1.70.s:
tanmātrāṇāṃ dvitīyastu bhūtasargaḥ sa ucyate
vaikārikastṛtīyastu sarga aindriyakaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.70.d:
तन्मात्राणां द्वितीयस्तु भूतसर्गः स उच्यते
वैकारिकस्तृतीयस्तु सर्ग ऐन्द्रियकः स्मृतः ॥
1.70.m: The second is that of the subtle elements (tanmātra), called the creation of the elements (bhūtasarga). / The third, modified (vaikārika), is remembered as the creation of the senses (aindriyaka).

1.70.s:
ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargaḥ sambhūto buddhipūrvakaḥ
mukhyasargaścaturthaś ca mukhyā vai sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
इत्येष प्राकृतः सर्गः सम्भूतो बुद्धिपूर्वकः
मुख्यसर्गश्चतुर्थश् च मुख्या वै स्थावराः स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: Thus this primary creation arose through intellect. / The fourth is the primary creation (mukhyasarga); the immovable beings are considered primary.

1.70.s:
tato 'rvāksrotasāṃ sargaḥ saptamaḥ sa tu mānuṣaḥ
aṣṭamo 'nugrahaḥ sargaḥ sāttvikastāmasaś ca saḥ //
1.70.d:
ततो ऽर्वाक्स्रोतसां सर्गः सप्तमः स तु मानुषः
अष्टमो ऽनुग्रहः सर्गः सात्त्विकस्तामसश् च सः ॥
1.70.m: Then the seventh is the creation of the downward-current beings, which is the human creation. / The eighth is the creation of grace, both sāttvika and tāmasa.

1.70.s:
pañcaite vaikṛtāḥ sargāḥ prākṛtāstu trayaḥ smṛtāḥ
prākṛto vaikṛtaścaiva kaumāro navamaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.70.d:
पञ्चैते वैकृताः सर्गाः प्राकृतास्तु त्रयः स्मृताः
प्राकृतो वैकृतश्चैव कौमारो नवमः स्मृतः ॥
1.70.m: These five are the secondary creations, and the primary creations are considered to be three. / Both primary and secondary is the Kaumāra creation, remembered as the ninth.

1.70.s:
abuddhipūrvakāḥ sargāḥ prākṛtāstu trayaḥ smṛtāḥ
buddhipūrvaṃ pravartante ṣaṭ punarbrahmaṇastu te //
1.70.d:
अबुद्धिपूर्वकाः सर्गाः प्राकृतास्तु त्रयः स्मृताः
बुद्धिपूर्वं प्रवर्तन्ते षट् पुनर्ब्रह्मणस्तु ते ॥
1.70.m: The three primary creations are remembered as proceeding without forethought; / the other six of Brahmā proceed with forethought.

1.70.s:
vistarānugrahaḥ sargaḥ kīrtyamāno nibodhata
caturdhāvasthitaḥ so 'tha sarvabhūteṣu kṛtsnaśaḥ //
1.70.d:
विस्तरानुग्रहः सर्गः कीर्त्यमानो निबोधत
चतुर्धावस्थितः सो ऽथ सर्वभूतेषु कृत्स्नशः ॥
1.70.m: Understand now the creation of grace in its detail as it is proclaimed: / it exists in four forms entirely among all living beings.

1.70.s:
ityete prākṛtāścaiva vaikṛtāś ca nava smṛtāḥ
parasparānuraktāś ca kāraṇaiś ca budhaiḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
इत्येते प्राकृताश्चैव वैकृताश् च नव स्मृताः
परस्परानुरक्ताश् च कारणैश् च बुधैः स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: Thus these primary and secondary creations are considered to be nine. / They are mutually attached, and considered by the wise to be bound by causes.

1.70.s:
agre sasarja vai brahmā mānasānātmanaḥ samān
ṛbhuḥ sanatkumāraś ca dvāvetāvūrdhvaretasau //
1.70.d:
अग्रे ससर्ज वै ब्रह्मा मानसानात्मनः समान्
ऋभुः सनत्कुमारश् च द्वावेतावूर्ध्वरेतसौ ॥
1.70.m: In the beginning Brahmā created mind-born [sons] equal to himself: / Ṛbhu and Sanatkumāra, these two of celibate vows.

1.70.s:
pūrvotpannau purā tebhyaḥ sarveṣāmapi pūrvajau
vyatīte tvaṣṭame kalpe purāṇau lokasākṣiṇau //
1.70.d:
पूर्वोत्पन्नौ पुरा तेभ्यः सर्वेषामपि पूर्वजौ
व्यतीते त्वष्टमे कल्पे पुराणौ लोकसाक्षिणौ ॥
1.70.m: Born before them in ancient times, eldest of all, / the ancient witnesses of the world, when the eighth kalpa had passed,

1.70.s:
tau vārāhe tu bhūrloke tejaḥ saṃkṣipya dhiṣṭhitau
tāvubhau mokṣakarmāṇāv āropyātmānamātmani //
1.70.d:
तौ वाराहे तु भूर्लोके तेजः संक्षिप्य धिष्ठितौ
तावुभौ मोक्षकर्माणाव् आरोप्यात्मानमात्मनि ॥
1.70.m: the two of them remained on the earth in the Vārāha [kalpa], withdrawing their splendour. / Both engaged in acts of liberation, establishing the self in the Self,

1.70.s:
prajāṃ dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca tyaktvā vairāgyamāsthitau
yathotpannastathaiveha kumāraḥ sa ihocyate //
1.70.d:
प्रजां धर्मं च कामं च त्यक्त्वा वैराग्यमास्थितौ
यथोत्पन्नस्तथैवेह कुमारः स इहोच्यते ॥
1.70.m: having abandoned progeny, duty, and desire, they resorted to detachment. / Because he remains just as he was born, he is called Kumāra (a boy) in this world;

1.70.s:
tasmāt sanatkumāreti nāmāsyeha prakīrtitam
sanandaṃ sanakaṃ caiva vidvāṃsaṃ ca sanātanam //
1.70.d:
तस्मात् सनत्कुमारेति नामास्येह प्रकीर्तितम्
सनन्दं सनकं चैव विद्वांसं च सनातनम् ॥
1.70.m: therefore his name is proclaimed here as Sanatkumāra. / [He created also] Sananda, Sanaka, and the wise Sanātana.

1.70.s:
vijñānena nivṛttāste vyavartanta mahaujasaḥ
saṃbuddhāścaiva nānātve apravṛttāś ca yoginaḥ //
1.70.d:
विज्ञानेन निवृत्तास्ते व्यवर्तन्त महौजसः
संबुद्धाश्चैव नानात्वे अप्रवृत्ताश् च योगिनः ॥
1.70.m: Through spiritual knowledge they were dispassionate, turning away, endowed with great splendour; / fully awakened to the diversity [of existence], those yogins did not engage [in procreation].

1.70.s:
asṛṣṭvaiva prajāsargaṃ pratisargaṃ gatāḥ punaḥ
tatasteṣu vyatīteṣu tato 'nyān sādhakān sutān //
1.70.d:
असृष्ट्वैव प्रजासर्गं प्रतिसर्गं गताः पुनः
ततस्तेषु व्यतीतेषु ततो ऽन्यान् साधकान् सुतान् ॥
1.70.m: Without producing the creation of progeny, they departed into secondary dissolution. / When they had passed away, Brahmā created other effective sons,

1.70.s:
mānasānasṛjadbrahmā punaḥ sthānābhimāninaḥ
ā bhūtasamplavāvasthā yairiyaṃ vidhṛtā mahī //
1.70.d:
मानसानसृजद्ब्रह्मा पुनः स्थानाभिमानिनः
आ भूतसम्प्लवावस्था यैरियं विधृता मही ॥
1.70.m: mind-born sons who identified with their stations, / by whom this earth is upheld until the state of the dissolution of beings.

1.70.s:
āpo 'gniṃ pṛthivīṃ vāyum antarikṣaṃ divaṃ tathā
samudrāṃś ca nadīścaiva tathā śailavanaspatīn //
1.70.d:
आपो ऽग्निं पृथिवीं वायुम् अन्तरिक्षं दिवं तथा
समुद्रांश् च नदीश्चैव तथा शैलवनस्पतीन् ॥
1.70.m: The waters, fire, earth, wind, the intermediate space, and the sky, / the oceans, the rivers, and likewise mountains and trees;

1.70.s:
oṣadhīnāṃ tathātmāno vallīnāṃ vṛkṣavīrudhām
latāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ kalāścaiva muhūrtāḥ saṃdhirātryahān //
1.70.d:
ओषधीनां तथात्मानो वल्लीनां वृक्षवीरुधाम्
लताः काष्ठाः कलाश्चैव मुहूर्ताः संधिरात्र्यहान् ॥
1.70.m: The presiding spirits of medicinal herbs, creepers, trees, and plants; / creepers, kāṣṭhās, kalās, muhūrtas, twilights, nights, and days;

1.70.s:
ardhamāsāṃś ca māsāṃś ca ayanābdayugāni ca
sthānābhimāninaḥ sarve sthānākhyāścaiva te smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
अर्धमासांश् च मासांश् च अयनाब्दयुगानि च
स्थानाभिमानिनः सर्वे स्थानाख्याश्चैव ते स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: Half-months, months, solstices, years, and yugas; / all these are remembered as presiding spirits of spheres, named after their spheres.

1.70.s:
devānṛṣīṃś ca mahato gadatastān nibodhata
marīcibhṛgvaṅgirasaṃ pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum //
1.70.d:
देवानृषींश् च महतो गदतस्तान् निबोधत
मरीचिभृग्वङ्गिरसं पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम् ॥
1.70.m: Listen as I speak of the gods and the great ṛṣis: / Marīci, Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu,

1.70.s:
dakṣamatriṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ ca so 'sṛjanmānasān nava
nava brahmāṇa ityete purāṇe niścayaṃ gatāḥ //
1.70.d:
दक्षमत्रिं वसिष्ठं च सो ऽसृजन्मानसान् नव
नव ब्रह्माण इत्येते पुराणे निश्चयं गताः ॥
1.70.m: Dakṣa, Atri, and Vasiṣṭha—he created these nine mind-born [sons]. / In the Purāṇa it is established that these are the nine Brahmās.

1.70.s:
teṣāṃ brahmātmakānāṃ vai sarveṣāṃ brahmavādinām
sthānāni kalpayāmāsa pūrvavatpadmasaṃbhavaḥ //
1.70.d:
तेषां ब्रह्मात्मकानां वै सर्वेषां ब्रह्मवादिनाम्
स्थानानि कल्पयामास पूर्ववत्पद्मसंभवः ॥
1.70.m: For all these exponents of the Veda, whose nature was identical with Brahman, / the lotus-born [Brahmā] appointed spheres as before.

1.70.s:
tato 'sṛjacca saṃkalpaṃ dharmaṃ caiva sukhāvaham
so 'sṛjad vyavasāyāttu dharmaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ //
1.70.d:
ततो ऽसृजच्च संकल्पं धर्मं चैव सुखावहम्
सो ऽसृजद् व्यवसायात्तु धर्मं देवो महेश्वरः ॥
1.70.m: Then he created Intention (Saṅkalpa) and Dharma, the bringer of happiness; / indeed, the god Maheśvara created Dharma from his resolve (vyavasāya),

1.70.s:
saṃkalpaṃ caiva saṃkalpāt sarvalokapitāmahaḥ
mānasaś ca rucirnāma vijajñe brahmaṇaḥ prabhoḥ //
1.70.d:
संकल्पं चैव संकल्पात् सर्वलोकपितामहः
मानसश् च रुचिर्नाम विजज्ञे ब्रह्मणः प्रभोः ॥
1.70.m: And Intention from his intention, as the Grandfather of all the worlds. / And from the mind of the lord Brahmā, the one named Ruci was born.

1.70.s:
prāṇādbrahmāsṛjaddakṣaṃ cakṣurbhyāṃ ca marīcinam
bhṛgustu hṛdayājjajñe ṛṣiḥ salilajanmanaḥ //
1.70.d:
प्राणाद्ब्रह्मासृजद्दक्षं चक्षुर्भ्यां च मरीचिनम्
भृगुस्तु हृदयाज्जज्ञे ऋषिः सलिलजन्मनः ॥
1.70.m: From his breath Brahmā created Dakṣa, and Marīci from his two eyes; / the sage Bhṛgu was born from the heart of the water-born one.

1.70.s:
śiraso 'ṅgirasaścaiva śrotrādatriṃ tathāsṛjat
pulastyaṃ ca tathodānād vyānācca pulahaṃ punaḥ //
1.70.d:
शिरसो ऽङ्गिरसश्चैव श्रोत्रादत्रिं तथासृजत्
पुलस्त्यं च तथोदानाद् व्यानाच्च पुलहं पुनः ॥
1.70.m: From his head [he created] Aṅgiras, and from his ear he created Atri; / likewise Pulastya from the udāna breath, and Pulaha from the vyāna;

1.70.s:
samānajo vasiṣṭhaś ca apānānnirmame kratum
ityete brahmaṇaḥ putrā divyā ekādaśā smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
समानजो वसिष्ठश् च अपानान्निर्ममे क्रतुम्
इत्येते ब्रह्मणः पुत्रा दिव्या एकादशा स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: Vasiṣṭha was born from the samāna, and Kratu he fashioned from the apāna. / These are remembered as the eleven celestial sons of Brahmā.

1.70.s:
dharmādayaḥ prathamajāḥ sarve te brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ
bhṛgvādayastu te sṛṣṭā navaite brahmavādinaḥ //
1.70.d:
धर्मादयः प्रथमजाः सर्वे ते ब्रह्मणः सुताः
भृग्वादयस्तु ते सृष्टा नवैते ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥
1.70.m: Dharma and the others were the firstborn; all of them were sons of Brahmā. / But these nine exponents of the Veda, Bhṛgu and the others, were created [next].

1.70.s:
gṛhamedhinaḥ purāṇās te dharmas taiḥ sampravartitaḥ
teṣāṃ dvādaśa te vaṃśā divyā devaguṇānvitāḥ //
1.70.d:
गृहमेधिनः पुराणास् ते धर्मस् तैः सम्प्रवर्तितः
तेषां द्वादश ते वंशा दिव्या देवगुणान्विताः ॥
1.70.m: They were ancient householders, by whom Dharma was set in motion; / their lineages are twelve, celestial and endowed with divine qualities,

1.70.s:
kriyāvantaḥ prajāvanto maharṣibhir alaṃkṛtāḥ
ṛbhuḥ sanatkumāraś ca dvāvetāvūrdhvaretasau //
1.70.d:
क्रियावन्तः प्रजावन्तो महर्षिभिर् अलंकृताः
ऋभुः सनत्कुमारश् च द्वावेतावूर्ध्वरेतसौ ॥
1.70.m: Performing rites, endowed with offspring, and adorned by great ṛṣis. / Ṛbhu and Sanatkumāra—these two were celibates.

1.70.s:
pūrvotpannau paraṃ tebhyaḥ sarveṣāmapi pūrvajau
vyatīte tvaṣṭame kalpe purāṇau lokasākṣiṇau //
1.70.d:
पूर्वोत्पन्नौ परं तेभ्यः सर्वेषामपि पूर्वजौ
व्यतीते त्वष्टमे कल्पे पुराणौ लोकसाक्षिणौ ॥
1.70.m: Though born before them, higher than them, and the eldest of all, / when the eighth kalpa had passed, those two ancient witnesses of the world

1.70.s:
virājetāmubhau loke tejaḥ saṃkṣipya dhiṣṭhitau
tāvubhau yogakarmāṇāv āropyātmānam ātmani //
1.70.d:
विराजेतामुभौ लोके तेजः संक्षिप्य धिष्ठितौ
तावुभौ योगकर्माणाव् आरोप्यात्मानम् आत्मनि ॥
1.70.m: Shone forth in the world, abiding there with their splendour drawn inward. / Both engaged in the practice of yoga, fixing the self within the Self,

1.70.s:
prajāṃ dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca tyaktvā vairāgyamāsthitau
yathotpannaḥ sa eveha kumāraḥ sa ihocyate //
1.70.d:
प्रजां धर्मं च कामं च त्यक्त्वा वैराग्यमास्थितौ
यथोत्पन्नः स एवेह कुमारः स इहोच्यते ॥
1.70.m: Renouncing offspring, virtue, and desire, they resorted to dispassion. / As he was born, just so he remained a youth (kumāra); thus he is called here.

1.70.s:
tasmātsanatkumāreti nāmāsyeha pratiṣṭhitam
tato 'bhidhyāyatastasya jajñire mānasāḥ prajāḥ //
1.70.d:
तस्मात्सनत्कुमारेति नामास्येह प्रतिष्ठितम्
ततो ऽभिध्यायतस्तस्य जज्ञिरे मानसाः प्रजाः ॥
1.70.m: Therefore his name is established here as Sanatkumāra. / Then, as he meditated, mind-born creatures were born.

1.70.s:
taccharīrasamutpannaiḥ kāryaistaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ saha
kṣetrajñāḥ samavartanta gātrebhyastasya dhīmataḥ //
1.70.d:
तच्छरीरसमुत्पन्नैः कार्यैस्तैः कारणैः सह
क्षेत्रज्ञाः समवर्तन्त गात्रेभ्यस्तस्य धीमतः ॥
1.70.m: Together with effects and causes born from that body of his, / the knowers of the field arose from the limbs of that wise one.

1.70.s:
tato devāsurapitṝn mānuṣāṃś ca catuṣṭayam
sisṛkṣur ambhāṃsyetāni svam ātmānam ayūyujat //
1.70.d:
ततो देवासुरपितॄन् मानुषांश् च चतुष्टयम्
सिसृक्षुर् अम्भांस्येतानि स्वम् आत्मानम् अयूयुजत् ॥
1.70.m: Then, desiring to create the fourfold [group]—gods, asuras, ancestors, and men— / he applied himself to these waters (ambhāṃsi).

1.70.s:
tatastu yuñjatastasya tamomātrasamudbhavam
samabhidhyāyataḥ sargaṃ prayatnena prajāpateḥ //
1.70.d:
ततस्तु युञ्जतस्तस्य तमोमात्रसमुद्भवम्
समभिध्यायतः सर्गं प्रयत्नेन प्रजापतेः ॥
1.70.m: Then, as he applied himself to that creation born solely of tamas, / meditating with effort, the lord of creatures [became engrossed].

1.70.s:
tato 'sya jaghanātpūrvam asurā jajñire sutāḥ
asuḥ prāṇaḥ smṛto viprās tajjanmānas tato 'surāḥ //
1.70.d:
ततो ऽस्य जघनात्पूर्वम् असुरा जज्ञिरे सुताः
असुः प्राणः स्मृतो विप्रास् तज्जन्मानस् ततो ऽसुराः ॥
1.70.m: Then, from his loins the asuras were first born as sons. / 'Asu' is known as vital breath, O brahmins; because they were born from that, they are asuras.

1.70.s:
yayā sṛṣṭāsurāḥ sarve tāṃ tanuṃ sa vyapohata
sāpaviddhā tanus tena sadyo rātrir ajāyata //
1.70.d:
यया सृष्टासुराः सर्वे तां तनुं स व्यपोहत
सापविद्धा तनुस् तेन सद्यो रात्रिर् अजायत ॥
1.70.m: That body by which all the asuras were created, he cast aside; / that body cast aside by him instantly became night.

1.70.s:
sā tamobahulā yasmāt tato rātrirniyāmikā
āvṛtāstamasā rātrau prajāstasmātsvapantyuta //
1.70.d:
सा तमोबहुला यस्मात् ततो रात्रिर्नियामिका
आवृतास्तमसा रात्रौ प्रजास्तस्मात्स्वपन्त्युत ॥
1.70.m: Because it abounds in tamas, night is therefore the regulator; / enveloped in tamas, creatures therefore sleep at night.

1.70.s:
sṛṣṭvāsurāṃstataḥ so vai tanumanyāmagṛhṇata
avyaktāṃ sattvabahulāṃ tatastāṃ so 'bhyapūjayat //
1.70.d:
सृष्ट्वासुरांस्ततः सो वै तनुमन्यामगृह्णत
अव्यक्तां सत्त्वबहुलां ततस्तां सो ऽभ्यपूजयत् ॥
1.70.m: Having created the asuras, he then assumed another body / that was unmanifest and abundant in sattva; then he worshipped it.

1.70.s:
tatastāṃ yuñjatas tasya priyam āsīt prajāpateḥ
tato mukhātsamutpannā dīvyatastasya devatāḥ //
1.70.d:
ततस्तां युञ्जतस् तस्य प्रियम् आसीत् प्रजापतेः
ततो मुखात्समुत्पन्ना दीव्यतस्तस्य देवताः ॥
1.70.m: Then, as he applied it, delight came to the lord of creatures; / then, as he played, deities were born from his mouth.

1.70.s:
yato 'sya dīvyato jātās tena devāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
dhāturdiviti yaḥ proktaḥ krīḍāyāṃ sa vibhāvyate //
1.70.d:
यतो ऽस्य दीव्यतो जातास् तेन देवाः प्रकीर्तिताः
धातुर्दिविति यः प्रोक्तः क्रीडायां स विभाव्यते ॥
1.70.m: Because they were born while he was playing (dīvyataḥ), they are therefore proclaimed as gods (devas); / the root 'div' that is taught is understood in the sense of 'to play'.

1.70.s:
yasmāttasya tu dīvyanto jajñire tena devatāḥ
devānsṛṣṭvātha deveśas tanumanyāmapadyata //
1.70.d:
यस्मात्तस्य तु दीव्यन्तो जज्ञिरे तेन देवताः
देवान्सृष्ट्वाथ देवेशस् तनुमन्यामपद्यत ॥
1.70.m: Because they were born shining (dīvyantaḥ) from him, they are deities (devatās). / Having created the gods, the lord of gods then assumed another body.

1.70.s:
utsṛṣṭā sā tanustena sadyo 'haḥ samajāyata
tasmādaho dharmayuktaṃ devatāḥ samupāsate //
1.70.d:
उत्सृष्टा सा तनुस्तेन सद्यो ऽहः समजायत
तस्मादहो धर्मयुक्तं देवताः समुपासते ॥
1.70.m: That body cast aside by him instantly became day; / therefore deities wait upon the day endowed with virtue.

1.70.s:
sattvamātrātmikāmeva tato 'nyāṃ so 'bhyamanyata
pitṛvanmanyamānasya putrāṃstāndhyāyataḥ prabhoḥ //
1.70.d:
सत्त्वमात्रात्मिकामेव ततो ऽन्यां सो ऽभ्यमन्यत
पितृवन्मन्यमानस्य पुत्रांस्तान्ध्यायतः प्रभोः ॥
1.70.m: Then he conceived another [body] consisting solely of sattva; / as the lord thought of them like a father, meditating on those sons,

1.70.s:
pitaro hyupapakṣābhyāṃ rātryahṇor antare 'bhavan
tasmātte pitaro devāḥ pitṛtvaṃ tena teṣu tat //
1.70.d:
पितरो ह्युपपक्षाभ्यां रात्र्यह्णोर् अन्तरे ऽभवन्
तस्मात्ते पितरो देवाः पितृत्वं तेन तेषु तत् ॥
1.70.m: The ancestors (pitaraḥ) were born from his sides, in the interval between night and day; / therefore those gods are ancestors, and that fatherhood pertains to them.

1.70.s:
yayā sṛṣṭāstu pitaras tanuṃ tāṃ sa vyapohata
sāpaviddhā tanustena sadyaḥ saṃdhyā vyajāyata //
1.70.d:
यया सृष्टास्तु पितरस् तनुं तां स व्यपोहत
सापविद्धा तनुस्तेन सद्यः संध्या व्यजायत ॥
1.70.m: That body by which the ancestors were created, he cast aside; / that body cast aside by him instantly became twilight.

1.70.s:
yasmādahardevatānāṃ rātriryā sāsurī smṛtā
tayormadhye tu paitrī yā tanuḥ sā tu garīyasī //
1.70.d:
यस्मादहर्देवतानां रात्रिर्या सासुरी स्मृता
तयोर्मध्ये तु पैत्री या तनुः सा तु गरीयसी ॥
1.70.m: Because day belongs to the deities, and night is known to belong to the asuras, / between the two, that ancestral body is weightier.

1.70.s:
tasmāddevā surāḥ sarve ṛṣayo mānavās tathā
upāsante mudāyuktā rātryahṇor madhyamāṃ tanum //
1.70.d:
तस्माद्देवा सुराः सर्वे ऋषयो मानवास् तथा
उपासन्ते मुदायुक्ता रात्र्यह्णोर् मध्यमां तनुम् ॥
1.70.m: Therefore all the gods, asuras, ṛṣis, and men / worship, filled with joy, that middle body between night and day.

1.70.s:
tato hyanyāṃ punarbrahmā tanuṃ vai samagṛhṇata
rajomātrātmikāyāṃ tu manasā so 'sṛjatprabhuḥ //
1.70.d:
ततो ह्यन्यां पुनर्ब्रह्मा तनुं वै समगृह्णत
रजोमात्रात्मिकायां तु मनसा सो ऽसृजत्प्रभुः ॥
1.70.m: Then Brahmā indeed assumed yet another body; / in that one consisting solely of rajas, the lord created with his mind.

1.70.s:
rajaḥpriyāṃstataḥ so 'tha mānasānasṛjatsutān
manasvinastatastasya mānavā jajñire sutāḥ //
1.70.d:
रजःप्रियांस्ततः सो ऽथ मानसानसृजत्सुतान्
मनस्विनस्ततस्तस्य मानवा जज्ञिरे सुताः ॥
1.70.m: Then he created mind-born sons who took delight in rajas; / then the sons who were intelligent men (mānavas) were born to him.

1.70.s:
sṛṣṭvā punaḥ prajāścāpi svāṃ tanuṃ tām apohata
sāpaviddhā tanustena jyotsnā sadyastvajāyata //
1.70.d:
सृष्ट्वा पुनः प्रजाश्चापि स्वां तनुं ताम् अपोहत
सापविद्धा तनुस्तेन ज्योत्स्ना सद्यस्त्वजायत ॥
1.70.m: And having created those beings, he also cast aside that body of his; / that body cast aside by him instantly became moonlight (jyotsnā).

1.70.s:
yasmādbhavanti saṃhṛṣṭā jyotsnāyā udbhave prajāḥ
ityetāstanavastena hy apaviddhā mahātmanā //
1.70.d:
यस्माद्भवन्ति संहृष्टा ज्योत्स्नाया उद्भवे प्रजाः
इत्येतास्तनवस्तेन ह्य् अपविद्धा महात्मना ॥
1.70.m: Because creatures become delighted upon the rise of moonlight, / these bodies were thus cast aside by that great soul.

1.70.s:
sadyo rātryahanī caiva saṃdhyā jyotsnā ca jajñire
jyotsnā saṃdhyā ahaścaiva sattvamātrātmakaṃ trayam //
1.70.d:
सद्यो रात्र्यहनी चैव संध्या ज्योत्स्ना च जज्ञिरे
ज्योत्स्ना संध्या अहश्चैव सत्त्वमात्रात्मकं त्रयम् ॥
1.70.m: Instantly night, day, twilight, and moonlight were born; / moonlight, twilight, and day—this triad consists solely of sattva.

1.70.s:
tamomātrātmikā rātriḥ sā vai tasmānniśātmikā
tasmāddevā divātanvā tuṣṭyā sṛṣṭā mukhāttu vai //
1.70.d:
तमोमात्रात्मिका रात्रिः सा वै तस्मान्निशात्मिका
तस्माद्देवा दिवातन्वा तुष्ट्या सृष्टा मुखात्तु वै ॥
1.70.m: Night consists solely of tamas, and therefore it is of the nature of darkness; / therefore the gods were created from the mouth by day-body through satisfaction.

1.70.s:
yasmātteṣāṃ divā janma balinastena vai divā
tanvā yayāsurān rātrau jaghanādasṛjatprabhuḥ //
1.70.d:
यस्मात्तेषां दिवा जन्म बलिनस्तेन वै दिवा
तन्वा ययासुरान् रात्रौ जघनादसृजत्प्रभुः ॥
1.70.m: Because their birth took place by day, they are powerful by day; / with that body by which the lord created the asuras at night from his loins,

1.70.s:
prāṇebhyo niśijanmāno balino niśi tena te
etānyeva bhaviṣyāṇāṃ devānāmasuraiḥ saha //
1.70.d:
प्राणेभ्यो निशिजन्मानो बलिनो निशि तेन ते
एतान्येव भविष्याणां देवानामसुरैः सह ॥
1.70.m: Born from the vital breaths at night, they are therefore powerful at night. / These very [bodies] are the causes for future gods and asuras,

1.70.s:
pitṝṇāṃ mānavānāṃ ca atītānāgateṣu vai
manvantareṣu sarveṣu nimittāni bhavanti hi //
1.70.d:
पितॄणां मानवानां च अतीतानागतेषु वै
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु निमित्तानि भवन्ति हि ॥
1.70.m: And for ancestors and men, in all manvantaras, / both past and future.

1.70.s:
jyotsnā rātryahanī saṃdhyā catvāryaṃbhāṃsi tāni vai
bhānti yasmāt tato 'ṃbhāṃsi śabdo 'yaṃ sumanīṣibhiḥ //
1.70.d:
ज्योत्स्ना रात्र्यहनी संध्या चत्वार्यंभांसि तानि वै
भान्ति यस्मात् ततो ऽंभांसि शब्दो ऽयं सुमनीषिभिः ॥
1.70.m: Moonlight, night, day, and twilight are indeed those four 'waters' (ambhāṃsi); / because they shine (bhānti), this word 'ambhāṃsi' is used by the wise.

1.70.s:
bhātirdīptau nigaditaḥ punaścātha prajāpatiḥ
so 'mbhāṃsyetāni sṛṣṭvā tu devamānuṣadānavān //
1.70.d:
भातिर्दीप्तौ निगदितः पुनश्चाथ प्रजापतिः
सो ऽम्भांस्येतानि सृष्ट्वा तु देवमानुषदानवान् ॥
1.70.m: The verbal root 'bhā' is declared in the sense of shining. And then again the lord of creatures, / having created these waters, [created] gods, men, and dānavas.

1.70.s:
pitṝṃścaiva sṛjattanvā ātmanā vividhānpunaḥ
tāmutsṛjya tanuṃ jyotsnāṃ tato 'nyāṃ prāpya sa prabhuḥ //
1.70.d:
पितॄंश्चैव सृजत्तन्वा आत्मना विविधान्पुनः
तामुत्सृज्य तनुं ज्योत्स्नां ततो ऽन्यां प्राप्य स प्रभुः ॥
1.70.m: And he created the ancestors, manifold again, through his body by himself. / Having cast aside that moonlight body, the lord obtained another,

1.70.s:
mūrtiṃ tamorajaḥprāyāṃ punarevābhyapūjayat
andhakāre kṣudhāviṣṭāṃs tato 'nyān so 'sṛjat prabhuḥ //
1.70.d:
मूर्तिं तमोरजःप्रायां पुनरेवाभ्यपूजयत्
अन्धकारे क्षुधाविष्टांस् ततो ऽन्यान् सो ऽसृजत् प्रभुः ॥
1.70.m: A form composed mostly of tamas and rajas, which he worshipped again; / then, in the darkness, the lord created others who were overcome by hunger.

1.70.s:
tena sṛṣṭāḥ kṣudhātmāno aṃbhāṃsyādātum udyatāḥ
ambhāṃsyetāni rakṣāma uktavantastu teṣu ye //
1.70.d:
तेन सृष्टाः क्षुधात्मानो अंभांस्यादातुम् उद्यताः
अम्भांस्येतानि रक्षाम उक्तवन्तस्तु तेषु ये ॥
1.70.m: Created by him, being hungry by nature, they set about seizing the waters; / among them, those who said, 'Let us protect (rakṣāmaḥ) these waters,' [became rākṣasas].

1.70.s:
rākṣasā nāma te yasmāt kṣudhāviṣṭā niśācarāḥ
ye 'bruvan yakṣamo 'mbhāṃsi teṣāṃ hṛṣṭāḥ parasparam //
1.70.d:
राक्षसा नाम ते यस्मात् क्षुधाविष्टा निशाचराः
ये ऽब्रुवन् यक्षमो ऽम्भांसि तेषां हृष्टाः परस्परम् ॥
1.70.m: Because they were overcome by hunger, those night-wanderers were called Rākṣasas. / Those among them who, rejoicing among themselves, said, “We shall eat (yakṣāmaḥ) the waters”,

1.70.s:
tena te karmaṇā yakṣā guhyakā gūḍhakarmaṇā
rakṣeti pālane cāpi dhātureṣa vibhāṣyate //
1.70.d:
तेन ते कर्मणा यक्षा गुह्यका गूढकर्मणा
रक्षेति पालने चापि धातुरेष विभाष्यते ॥
1.70.m: Because of that action, they became Yakṣas, and Guhyakas due to their hidden action (gūḍhakarma). / The root rakṣ- is declared in the sense of protecting,

1.70.s:
evaṃ ca yakṣatir dhātur bhakṣaṇe sa nirucyate
taṃ dṛṣṭvā hyapriyeṇāsya keśāḥ śīrṇāstu dhīmataḥ //
1.70.d:
एवं च यक्षतिर् धातुर् भक्षणे स निरुच्यते
तं दृष्ट्वा ह्यप्रियेणास्य केशाः शीर्णास्तु धीमतः ॥
1.70.m: And likewise the root yakṣ- is explained in the sense of eating. / Seeing this, the hairs of that wise [creator] fell out from displeasure.

1.70.s:
te śīrṇāścotthitā hyūrdhvaṃ te caivārurudhuḥ prabhum
hīnāstacchiraso vālā yasmāccaivāvasarpiṇaḥ //
1.70.d:
ते शीर्णाश्चोत्थिता ह्यूर्ध्वं ते चैवारुरुधुः प्रभुम्
हीनास्तच्छिरसो वाला यस्माच्चैवावसर्पिणः ॥
1.70.m: Having fallen, they rose upward and indeed obstructed the Lord. / Because the hairs fell down from his head and crept along (avasarpiṇaḥ),

1.70.s:
vyālātmānaḥ smṛtā vālā hīnatvādahayaḥ smṛtāḥ
patatvātpannagāścaiva sarpāścaivāvasarpaṇāt //
1.70.d:
व्यालात्मानः स्मृता वाला हीनत्वादहयः स्मृताः
पतत्वात्पन्नगाश्चैव सर्पाश्चैवावसर्पणात् ॥
1.70.m: Hairs (vālāḥ) are known as snakes (vyālāḥ), and from their fallen state (hīnatva) they are called ahis; / From falling (patana) they are pannagas, and from creeping (avasarpaṇa) they are sarpas.

1.70.s:
tasya krodhodbhavo yo 'sau agnigarbhaḥ sudāruṇaḥ
sa tu sarpān sahotpannān āviveśa viṣātmakaḥ //
1.70.d:
तस्य क्रोधोद्भवो यो ऽसौ अग्निगर्भः सुदारुणः
स तु सर्पान् सहोत्पन्नान् आविवेश विषात्मकः ॥
1.70.m: That which arose from his anger, terrible, containing fire within, / Entered those serpents born at that very moment, becoming their venom.

1.70.s:
sarpānsṛṣṭvā tataḥ kruddhaḥ krodhātmāno vinirmame
varṇena kapiśenogrās te bhūtāḥ piśitāśanāḥ //
1.70.d:
सर्पान्सृष्ट्वा ततः क्रुद्धः क्रोधात्मानो विनिर्ममे
वर्णेन कपिशेनोग्रास् ते भूताः पिशिताशनाः ॥
1.70.m: Then, having created the serpents, the enraged one fashioned beings made of anger: / Fierce, tawny-brown in colour, flesh-eating beings (bhūtas).

1.70.s:
bhūtatvātte smṛtā bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ piśitāśanāt
prasannaṃ gāyatastasya gandharvā jajñire yadā //
1.70.d:
भूतत्वात्ते स्मृता भूताः पिशाचाः पिशिताशनात्
प्रसन्नं गायतस्तस्य गन्धर्वा जज्ञिरे यदा ॥
1.70.m: From their being brought forth (bhūtatva) they are called Bhūtas, and Piśācas from eating raw flesh (piśitāśana). / When, as he sang delightfully, the Gandharvas were born,

1.70.s:
dhayatītyeṣa vai dhātuḥ pānatve paripaṭhyate
dhayanto jajñire vācaṃ gandharvāstena te smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
धयतीत्येष वै धातुः पानत्वे परिपठ्यते
धयन्तो जज्ञिरे वाचं गन्धर्वास्तेन ते स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: The root dhā- is recited in the sense of drinking; / Drinking speech, they were born, and therefore they are known as Gandharvas.

1.70.s:
aṣṭasvetāsu sṛṣṭāsu devayoniṣu sa prabhuḥ
tataḥ svacchandato 'nyāni vayāṃsi vayasāsṛjat //
1.70.d:
अष्टस्वेतासु सृष्टासु देवयोनिषु स प्रभुः
ततः स्वच्छन्दतो ऽन्यानि वयांसि वयसासृजत् ॥
1.70.m: When these eight classes of divine beings had been created, that Lord / Then, according to his will, created other flying creatures (vayāṃsi) through his vital age (vayas).

1.70.s:
svacchandataḥ svacchandāṃsi vayasā ca vayāṃsi ca
paśūnsṛṣṭvā sa deveśo 'sṛjatpakṣigaṇānapi //
1.70.d:
स्वच्छन्दतः स्वच्छन्दांसि वयसा च वयांसि च
पशून्सृष्ट्वा स देवेशो ऽसृजत्पक्षिगणानपि ॥
1.70.m: According to his will (svacchandataḥ) he created the meters (svacchandāṃsi), and through vital age (vayas) flying creatures (vayāṃsi). / Having created domestic animals, that Lord of gods also created the flocks of birds.

1.70.s:
mukhato 'jāḥ sasarjātha vakṣasaś cāvayo 'sṛjat
gāścaivāthodarādbrahmā pārśvābhyāṃ ca vinirmame //
1.70.d:
मुखतो ऽजाः ससर्जाथ वक्षसश् चावयो ऽसृजत्
गाश्चैवाथोदराद्ब्रह्मा पार्श्वाभ्यां च विनिर्ममे ॥
1.70.m: From his mouth he created goats, and from his chest he created sheep; / And Brahmā fashioned cows from his belly and his two flanks.

1.70.s:
padbhyāṃ cāśvān samātaṅgān rāsabhān āvayān mṛgān
uṣṭrānaśvatarāṃścaiva tathānyāścaiva jātayaḥ //
1.70.d:
पद्भ्यां चाश्वान् समातङ्गान् रासभान् आवयान् मृगान्
उष्ट्रानश्वतरांश्चैव तथान्याश्चैव जातयः ॥
1.70.m: From his feet [he created] horses, elephants, donkeys, sheep, deer, / Camels, and mules, as well as other species.

1.70.s:
oṣadhyaḥ phalamūlinyo romabhyastasya jajñire
evaṃ paśvoṣadhīḥ sṛṣṭvā yūyujat so 'dhvare prabhuḥ //
1.70.d:
ओषध्यः फलमूलिन्यो रोमभ्यस्तस्य जज्ञिरे
एवं पश्वोषधीः सृष्ट्वा यूयुजत् सो ऽध्वरे प्रभुः ॥
1.70.m: From his body-hairs sprang plants bearing fruit and roots. / Having thus created animals and plants, the Lord joined them to the sacrifice.

1.70.s:
gaurajaḥ pūruṣo meṣo hy aśvo 'śvataragardabhau
etāngrāmyānpaśūnāhur āraṇyānvai nibodhata //
1.70.d:
गौरजः पूरुषो मेषो ह्य् अश्वो ऽश्वतरगर्दभौ
एतान्ग्राम्यान्पशूनाहुर् आरण्यान्वै निबोधत ॥
1.70.m: The cow, the goat, man, the sheep, the horse, the mule, and the donkey— / These they call domestic animals; now learn of the wild animals:

1.70.s:
śvāpado dvikhuro hastī vānarāḥ pakṣipañcamāḥ
audakāḥ paśavaḥ ṣaṣṭhāḥ saptamāstu sarīsṛpāḥ //
1.70.d:
श्वापदो द्विखुरो हस्ती वानराः पक्षिपञ्चमाः
औदकाः पशवः षष्ठाः सप्तमास्तु सरीसृपाः ॥
1.70.m: Carnivores, cloven-hoofed beasts, elephants, monkeys as the fifth, along with birds, / Aquatic animals as the sixth, and reptiles as the seventh.

1.70.s:
mahiṣā gavayākṣāś ca plavaṃgāḥ śarabhā vṛkāḥ
siṃhastu saptamasteṣām āraṇyāḥ paśavaḥ smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
महिषा गवयाक्षाश् च प्लवंगाः शरभा वृकाः
सिंहस्तु सप्तमस्तेषाम् आरण्याः पशवः स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: Buffaloes, gayals, bears, monkeys, śarabhas, wolves, / And the lion as the seventh among them: these are recorded as the wild animals.

1.70.s:
gāyatraṃ ca ṛcaṃ caiva trivṛtsāmarathaṃtaram
agniṣṭomaṃ ca yajñānāṃ nirmame prathamān mukhāt //
1.70.d:
गायत्रं च ऋचं चैव त्रिवृत्सामरथंतरम्
अग्निष्टोमं च यज्ञानां निर्ममे प्रथमान् मुखात् ॥
1.70.m: The Gāyatrī meter, the Ṛgveda, the Trivṛt-stoma, the Rathantara-sāman, / And the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice among rites, he fashioned from his first mouth.

1.70.s:
yajūṃṣi traiṣṭubhaṃ chandastomaṃ pañcadaśaṃ tathā
bṛhatsāma tathokthyaṃ ca dakṣiṇādasṛjanmukhāt //
1.70.d:
यजूंषि त्रैष्टुभं छन्दस्तोमं पञ्चदशं तथा
बृहत्साम तथोक्थ्यं च दक्षिणादसृजन्मुखात् ॥
1.70.m: The Yajurveda, the Triṣṭubh meter, the fifteenfold stoma, / The Bṛhat-sāman, and the Ukthya, he created from his southern mouth.

1.70.s:
sāmāni jagatīchandastomaṃ saptadaśaṃ tathā
vairūpamatirātraṃ ca paścimādasṛjanmukhāt //
1.70.d:
सामानि जगतीछन्दस्तोमं सप्तदशं तथा
वैरूपमतिरात्रं च पश्चिमादसृजन्मुखात् ॥
1.70.m: The Sāmaveda, the Jagatī meter, the seventeenfold stoma, / The Vairūpa-sāman, and the Atirātra sacrifice, he created from his western mouth.

1.70.s:
ekaviṃśamatharvāṇam āptoryāmāṇam eva ca
anuṣṭubhaṃ savairājam uttarādasṛjanmukhāt //
1.70.d:
एकविंशमथर्वाणम् आप्तोर्यामाणम् एव च
अनुष्टुभं सवैराजम् उत्तरादसृजन्मुखात् ॥
1.70.m: The twenty-onefold stoma, the Atharvaveda, the Āptoryāma sacrifice, / The Anuṣṭubh meter, and the Vairāja-sāman, he created from his northern mouth.

1.70.s:
vidyuto 'śanimeghāṃś ca rohitendradhanūṃṣi ca
tejāṃsi ca sasarjādau kalpasya bhagavānprabhuḥ //
1.70.d:
विद्युतो ऽशनिमेघांश् च रोहितेन्द्रधनूंषि च
तेजांसि च ससर्जादौ कल्पस्य भगवान्प्रभुः ॥
1.70.m: Lightning, thunderbolts, clouds, crimson-streaked rainbows, / And fiery lights, the Lord God created at the beginning of the kalpa.

1.70.s:
uccāvacāni bhūtāni gātrebhyastasya jajñire
brahmaṇastu prajāsargaṃ sṛjato hi prajāpateḥ //
1.70.d:
उच्चावचानि भूतानि गात्रेभ्यस्तस्य जज्ञिरे
ब्रह्मणस्तु प्रजासर्गं सृजतो हि प्रजापतेः ॥
1.70.m: High and low beings were born from the limbs / Of Brahmā, the lord of creatures, as he produced the creation of living beings.

1.70.s:
sṛṣṭvā catuṣṭayaṃ pūrvaṃ devāsuranarānpitṝn
tato 'sṛjat sa bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca //
1.70.d:
सृष्ट्वा चतुष्टयं पूर्वं देवासुरनरान्पितॄन्
ततो ऽसृजत् स भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥
1.70.m: Having created the fourfold group first—gods, asuras, humans, and ancestors— / He then created beings stationary and moving:

1.70.s:
yakṣānpiśācān gandharvāṃs tv athaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇān
narakinnararakṣāṃsi vayaḥpaśumṛgoragān //
1.70.d:
यक्षान्पिशाचान् गन्धर्वांस् त्व् अथैवाप्सरसां गणान्
नरकिन्नररक्षांसि वयःपशुमृगोरगान् ॥
1.70.m: Yakṣas, Piśācas, Gandharvas, and the hosts of Apsarases, / Humans, Kinnaras, Rākṣasas, birds, domestic beasts, wild animals, and serpents,

1.70.s:
avyayaṃ ca vyayaṃ cāpi yadidaṃ sthāṇujaṅgamam
teṣāṃ vai yāni karmāṇi prāksṛṣṭyāṃ pratipedire //
1.70.d:
अव्ययं च व्ययं चापि यदिदं स्थाणुजङ्गमम्
तेषां वै यानि कर्माणि प्राक्सृष्ट्यां प्रतिपेदिरे ॥
1.70.m: And whatever here is immovable and moving, imperishable and perishable. / Indeed, the actions they engaged in during the previous creation,

1.70.s:
tānyeva pratipadyante sṛjyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharme nṛtānṛte //
1.70.d:
तान्येव प्रतिपद्यन्ते सृज्यमानाः पुनः पुनः
हिंस्राहिंस्रे मृदुक्रूरे धर्माधर्मे नृतानृते ॥
1.70.m: Those very actions they pursue as they are created again and again: / Violent or non-violent, gentle or cruel, righteous or unrighteous, true or false.

1.70.s:
tadbhāvitāḥ prapadyante tasmāttattasya rocate
mahābhūteṣu sṛṣṭeṣu indriyārtheṣu mūrtiṣu //
1.70.d:
तद्भाविताः प्रपद्यन्ते तस्मात्तत्तस्य रोचते
महाभूतेषु सृष्टेषु इन्द्रियार्थेषु मूर्तिषु ॥
1.70.m: Impelled by that, they adopt them; therefore that [behaviour] pleases that [being]. / When the gross elements, objects of the senses, and bodies were created,

1.70.s:
viniyogaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ dhātaiva vyadadhāt svayam
kecitpuruṣakāraṃ tu prāhuḥ karma sumānavāḥ //
1.70.d:
विनियोगं च भूतानां धातैव व्यदधात् स्वयम्
केचित्पुरुषकारं तु प्राहुः कर्म सुमानवाः ॥
1.70.m: The Creator himself appointed the functions of beings. / Excellent men say action is human effort (puruṣakāra);

1.70.s:
daivamityapare viprāḥ svabhāvaṃ bhūtacintakāḥ
pauruṣaṃ karma daivaṃ ca phalavṛttisvabhāvataḥ //
1.70.d:
दैवमित्यपरे विप्राः स्वभावं भूतचिन्तकाः
पौरुषं कर्म दैवं च फलवृत्तिस्वभावतः ॥
1.70.m: Other wise men say it is destiny (daiva); thinkers on material nature say it is innate nature (svabhāva). / Human effort, action, and destiny exist from the nature of the development of fruits.

1.70.s:
na caikaṃ na pṛthagbhāvam adhikaṃ na tato viduḥ
etadevaṃ ca naikaṃ ca nāmabhedena nāpyubhe //
1.70.d:
न चैकं न पृथग्भावम् अधिकं न ततो विदुः
एतदेवं च नैकं च नामभेदेन नाप्युभे ॥
1.70.m: They do not know them as single, nor as separated, nor as higher than that; / This is so, and it is not single, nor are both merely a difference of name.

1.70.s:
karmasthā viṣamaṃ brūyuḥ sattvasthāḥ samadarśanāḥ
nāma rūpaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ kṛtānāṃ ca prapañcanam //
1.70.d:
कर्मस्था विषमं ब्रूयुः सत्त्वस्थाः समदर्शनाः
नाम रूपं च भूतानां कृतानां च प्रपञ्चनम् ॥
1.70.m: Those established in action speak of inequality; those established in sattva have equal vision. / The name and form of created beings, and the expansion of deeds,

1.70.s:
vedaśabdebhya evādau nirmame sa maheśvaraḥ
ṛṣīṇāṃ nāmadheyāni yāś ca vedeṣu vṛttayaḥ //
1.70.d:
वेदशब्देभ्य एवादौ निर्ममे स महेश्वरः
ऋषीणां नामधेयानि याश् च वेदेषु वृत्तयः ॥
1.70.m: He, Maheśvara, fashioned in the beginning from the words of the Veda alone; / The names of the ṛṣis, and the activities mentioned in the Vedas,

1.70.s:
śarvaryante prasūtānāṃ tānyevaibhyo dadātyajaḥ
evaṃvidhāḥ sṛṣṭayastu brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ //
1.70.d:
शर्वर्यन्ते प्रसूतानां तान्येवैभ्यो ददात्यजः
एवंविधाः सृष्टयस्तु ब्रह्मणो ऽव्यक्तजन्मनः ॥
1.70.m: Those very things the Unborn grants to them when they are born at the end of the night. / Such creations of Brahmā, whose birth is from the Unmanifest,

1.70.s:
śarvaryante pradṛśyante siddhimāśritya mānasīm
evaṃbhūtāni sṛṣṭāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca //
1.70.d:
शर्वर्यन्ते प्रदृश्यन्ते सिद्धिमाश्रित्य मानसीम्
एवंभूतानि सृष्टानि स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥
1.70.m: Are seen at the end of the night, relying on his mental perfection. / Thus were created beings, stationary and moving.

1.70.s:
yadāsya tāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭā na vyavardhanta sattamāḥ
tamomātrāvṛto brahmā tadā śokena duḥkhitaḥ //
1.70.d:
यदास्य ताः प्रजाः सृष्टा न व्यवर्धन्त सत्तमाः
तमोमात्रावृतो ब्रह्मा तदा शोकेन दुःखितः ॥
1.70.m: When those created offspring of his did not multiply, O best of men, / Brahmā, enveloped only by tamas, was then distressed with sorrow.

1.70.s:
tataḥ sa vidadhe buddhim arthaniścayagāminīm
athātmani samadrākṣīt tamomātrāṃ niyāmikām //
1.70.d:
ततः स विदधे बुद्धिम् अर्थनिश्चयगामिनीम्
अथात्मनि समद्राक्षीत् तमोमात्रां नियामिकाम् ॥
1.70.m: Then he directed his intellect toward discerning the truth of things; / Then within himself he perceived a measure of tamas acting as a constraint,

1.70.s:
rajaḥsattvaṃ parityajya vartamānāṃ svadharmataḥ
tataḥ sa tena duḥkhena duḥkhaṃ cakre jagatpatiḥ //
1.70.d:
रजःसत्त्वं परित्यज्य वर्तमानां स्वधर्मतः
ततः स तेन दुःखेन दुःखं चक्रे जगत्पतिः ॥
1.70.m: Operating according to its own nature, having set aside rajas and sattva. / Then the Lord of the universe, overcome by that grief, experienced sorrow.

1.70.s:
tamaś ca vyanudatpaścād rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamāvṛṇot
tattamaḥ pratinunnaṃ vai mithunaṃ samajāyata //
1.70.d:
तमश् च व्यनुदत्पश्चाद् रजः सत्त्वं तमावृणोत्
तत्तमः प्रतिनुन्नं वै मिथुनं समजायत ॥
1.70.m: Afterward he drove away tamas; rajas and sattva enveloped him. / From that tamas, driven back indeed, a pair arose:

1.70.s:
adharmastamaso jajñe hiṃsā śokādajāyata
tatastasminsamudbhūte mithune dāruṇātmike //
1.70.d:
अधर्मस्तमसो जज्ञे हिंसा शोकादजायत
ततस्तस्मिन्समुद्भूते मिथुने दारुणात्मिके ॥
1.70.m: Adharma was born from tamas, and violence (hiṃsā) was born from sorrow. / Then, when that pair of terrible nature had come into being,

1.70.s:
gatāsur bhagavān āsīt prītiś cainam aśiśriyat
svāṃ tanuṃ sa tato brahmā tāmapohata bhāsvarām //
1.70.d:
गतासुर् भगवान् आसीत् प्रीतिश् चैनम् अशिश्रियत्
स्वां तनुं स ततो ब्रह्मा तामपोहत भास्वराम् ॥
1.70.m: The Lord became breathless, and joy abandoned him. / Thereupon Brahmā cast off that luminous body of his.

1.70.s:
dvidhā kṛtvā svakaṃ deham ardhena puruṣo 'bhavat
ardhena nārī sā tasya śatarūpā vyajāyata //
1.70.d:
द्विधा कृत्वा स्वकं देहम् अर्धेन पुरुषो ऽभवत्
अर्धेन नारी सा तस्य शतरूपा व्यजायत ॥
1.70.m: Dividing his own body into two, he became a male with one half; / With the other half a woman, Śatarūpā, was born to him.

1.70.s:
prakṛtiṃ bhūtadhātrīṃ tāṃ kāmādvai sṛṣṭavānprabhuḥ
sā divaṃ pṛthivīṃ caiva mahimnā vyāpyadhiṣṭhitā //
1.70.d:
प्रकृतिं भूतधात्रीं तां कामाद्वै सृष्टवान्प्रभुः
सा दिवं पृथिवीं चैव महिम्ना व्याप्यधिष्ठिता ॥
1.70.m: The Lord created out of desire that Prakṛti, the bearer of beings; / She stood pervading heaven and earth with her greatness.

1.70.s:
brahmaṇaḥ sā tanuḥ pūrvā divamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati
yā tvardhātsṛjato nārī śatarūpā vyajāyata //
1.70.d:
ब्रह्मणः सा तनुः पूर्वा दिवमावृत्य तिष्ठति
या त्वर्धात्सृजतो नारी शतरूपा व्यजायत ॥
1.70.m: That previous body of Brahmā stands enveloping the sky; / But the woman who was born from the half as he created, Śatarūpā,

1.70.s:
sā devī niyutaṃ taptvā tapaḥ paramaduścaram
bhartāraṃ dīptayaśasaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyapadyata //
1.70.d:
सा देवी नियुतं तप्त्वा तपः परमदुश्चरम्
भर्तारं दीप्तयशसं पुरुषं प्रत्यपद्यत ॥
1.70.m: That goddess, having performed supreme, arduous asceticism for a hundred thousand years, / Obtained as her husband that man of radiant fame.

1.70.s:
sa vai svāyaṃbhuvaḥ pūrvaṃ puruṣo manurucyate
tasyaiva saptatiyugaṃ manvantaramihocyate //
1.70.d:
स वै स्वायंभुवः पूर्वं पुरुषो मनुरुच्यते
तस्यैव सप्ततियुगं मन्वन्तरमिहोच्यते ॥
1.70.m: He indeed was the first man, called Svāyambhuva Manu; / His manvantara is declared here to consist of seventy-one [four-yuga cycles].

1.70.s:
lebhe sa puruṣaḥ patnīṃ śatarūpām ayonijām
tayā sārdhaṃ sa ramate tasmātsā ratirucyate //
1.70.d:
लेभे स पुरुषः पत्नीं शतरूपाम् अयोनिजाम्
तया सार्धं स रमते तस्मात्सा रतिरुच्यते ॥
1.70.m: That man obtained Śatarūpā, who was not born from a womb, as his wife. / He took delight with her; therefore she is called Rati.

1.70.s:
prathamaḥ saṃprayogātmā kalpādau samapadyata
virājam asṛjad brahmā so 'bhavat puruṣo virāṭ //
1.70.d:
प्रथमः संप्रयोगात्मा कल्पादौ समपद्यत
विराजम् असृजद् ब्रह्मा सो ऽभवत् पुरुषो विराट् ॥
1.70.m: The first union came to pass at the beginning of the kalpa. / Brahmā created Virāj; he became the cosmic male, Virāṭ.

1.70.s:
samrāṭ ca śatarūpā vai vairājaḥ sa manuḥ smṛtaḥ
sa vairājaḥ prajāsargaṃ sasarja puruṣo manuḥ //
1.70.d:
सम्राट् च शतरूपा वै वैराजः स मनुः स्मृतः
स वैराजः प्रजासर्गं ससर्ज पुरुषो मनुः ॥
1.70.m: And Śatarūpā was Samrāṭ; he, the Vairāja, is known as Manu. / That Puruṣa Manu, born of Virāj, produced the creation of living beings.

1.70.s:
vairājātpuruṣād vīrāc chatarūpā vyajāyata
priyavratottānapādau putrau dvau lokasaṃmatau //
1.70.d:
वैराजात्पुरुषाद् वीराच् छतरूपा व्यजायत
प्रियव्रतोत्तानपादौ पुत्रौ द्वौ लोकसंमतौ ॥
1.70.m: From that heroic Puruṣa born of Virāj, Śatarūpā brought forth / two sons honoured by the world, Priyavrata and Uttānapāda,

1.70.s:
kanye dve ca mahābhāge yābhyāṃ jātā imāḥ prajāḥ
devī nāma tathākūtiḥ prasūtiścaiva te ubhe //
1.70.d:
कन्ये द्वे च महाभागे याभ्यां जाता इमाः प्रजाः
देवी नाम तथाकूतिः प्रसूतिश्चैव ते उभे ॥
1.70.m: and two fortunate daughters from whom these creatures were born: / they were named the goddess Ākūti and Prasūti.

1.70.s:
svāyaṃbhuvaḥ prasūtiṃ tu dakṣāya pradadau prabhuḥ
prāṇo dakṣa iti jñeyaḥ saṃkalpo manurucyate //
1.70.d:
स्वायंभुवः प्रसूतिं तु दक्षाय प्रददौ प्रभुः
प्राणो दक्ष इति ज्ञेयः संकल्पो मनुरुच्यते ॥
1.70.m: The lord born of the Self-born gave Prasūti to Dakṣa; / Dakṣa is to be understood as the vital breath, and Manu is said to be the resolve.

1.70.s:
ruceḥ prajāpateḥ so 'tha ākūtiṃ pratyapādayat
ākūtyāṃ mithunaṃ jajñe mānasasya ruceḥ śubham //
1.70.d:
रुचेः प्रजापतेः सो ऽथ आकूतिं प्रत्यपादयत्
आकूत्यां मिथुनं जज्ञे मानसस्य रुचेः शुभम् ॥
1.70.m: He then gave Ākūti to the Prajāpati Ruci; / upon Ākūti, an auspicious twin pair was born to the mind-born Ruci.

1.70.s:
yajñaś ca dakṣiṇā caiva yamalau saṃbabhūvatuḥ
yajñasya dakṣiṇāyāṃ tu putrā dvādaśa jajñire //
1.70.d:
यज्ञश् च दक्षिणा चैव यमलौ संबभूवतुः
यज्ञस्य दक्षिणायां तु पुत्रा द्वादश जज्ञिरे ॥
1.70.m: Yajña and Dakṣiṇā were born as twins; / and upon Dakṣiṇā twelve sons were born to Yajña.

1.70.s:
yāmā iti samākhyātā devāḥ svāyaṃbhuve 'ntare
etasya putrā yajñasya tasmādyāmāś ca te smṛtāḥ //
1.70.d:
यामा इति समाख्याता देवाः स्वायंभुवे ऽन्तरे
एतस्य पुत्रा यज्ञस्य तस्माद्यामाश् च ते स्मृताः ॥
1.70.m: They are celebrated as the gods called Yāmas in the Svāyambhuva manvantara; / they are sons of this Yajña, and therefore they are known as Yāmas.

1.70.s:
ajitaścaiva śukraś ca gaṇau dvau brahmaṇā kṛtau
yāmāḥ pūrvaṃ prajātā ye te 'bhavaṃstu divaukasaḥ //
1.70.d:
अजितश्चैव शुक्रश् च गणौ द्वौ ब्रह्मणा कृतौ
यामाः पूर्वं प्रजाता ये ते ऽभवंस्तु दिवौकसः ॥
1.70.m: The Ajitas and the Śukras were two groups created by Brahmā; / those Yāmas who were born first became sky-dwellers.

1.70.s:
svāyaṃbhuvasutāyāṃ tu prasūtyāṃ lokamātaraḥ
tasyāṃ kanyāścaturviṃśad dakṣas tvajanayat prabhuḥ //
1.70.d:
स्वायंभुवसुतायां तु प्रसूत्यां लोकमातरः
तस्यां कन्याश्चतुर्विंशद् दक्षस् त्वजनयत् प्रभुः ॥
1.70.m: Upon Prasūti, the daughter of the son of the Self-born, the mothers of the world, / the lord Dakṣa fathered twenty-four daughters.

1.70.s:
sarvāstāś ca mahābhāgāḥ sarvāḥ kamalalocanāḥ
bhogavatyaś ca tāḥ sarvāḥ sarvāstā yogamātaraḥ //
1.70.d:
सर्वास्ताश् च महाभागाः सर्वाः कमललोचनाः
भोगवत्यश् च ताः सर्वाः सर्वास्ता योगमातरः ॥
1.70.m: All of them were greatly fortunate, all were lotus-eyed, / all possessed great splendour, and all were mothers of yoga.

1.70.s:
sarvāś ca brahmavādinyaḥ sarvā viśvasya mātaraḥ
śraddhā lakṣmīrdhṛtistuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirmedhā kriyā tathā //
1.70.d:
सर्वाश् च ब्रह्मवादिन्यः सर्वा विश्वस्य मातरः
श्रद्धा लक्ष्मीर्धृतिस्तुष्टिः पुष्टिर्मेधा क्रिया तथा ॥
1.70.m: All were expositors of Brahman, all were mothers of the universe: / Śraddhā, Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Tuṣṭi, Puṣṭi, Medhā, and Kriyā,

1.70.s:
buddhirlajjā vapuḥ śāntiḥ siddhiḥ kīrtistrayodaśa
patnyarthaṃ pratijagrāha dharmo dākṣāyaṇīḥ prabhuḥ //
1.70.d:
बुद्धिर्लज्जा वपुः शान्तिः सिद्धिः कीर्तिस्त्रयोदश
पत्न्यर्थं प्रतिजग्राह धर्मो दाक्षायणीः प्रभुः ॥
1.70.m: Buddhi, Lajjā, Vapuḥ, Śānti, Siddhi, and Kīrti—these thirteen / daughters of Dakṣa the lord Dharma took as his wives.

1.70.s:
dārāṇyetāni vai tasya vihitāni svayaṃbhuvā
tābhyaḥ śiṣṭāyavīyasya ekādaśa sulocanāḥ //
1.70.d:
दाराण्येतानि वै तस्य विहितानि स्वयंभुवा
ताभ्यः शिष्टायवीयस्य एकादश सुलोचनाः ॥
1.70.m: These wives were assigned to him by the Self-born. / The remaining eleven younger than these, fair-eyed women,

1.70.s:
satī khyātyatha saṃbhūtiḥ smṛtiḥ prītiḥ kṣamā tathā
saṃnatiścānasūyā ca ūrjā svāhā svadhā tathā //
1.70.d:
सती ख्यात्यथ संभूतिः स्मृतिः प्रीतिः क्षमा तथा
संनतिश्चानसूया च ऊर्जा स्वाहा स्वधा तथा ॥
1.70.m: Satī, Khyāti, then Saṃbhūti, Smṛti, Prīti, and Kṣamā, / Saṃnati, Anasūyā, Ūrjā, Svāhā, and Svadhā,

1.70.s:
tās tathā pratyapadyanta punaranye maharṣayaḥ
rudro bhṛgur marīciś ca aṅgirāḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ //
1.70.d:
तास् तथा प्रत्यपद्यन्त पुनरन्ये महर्षयः
रुद्रो भृगुर् मरीचिश् च अङ्गिराः पुलहः क्रतुः ॥
1.70.m: were likewise accepted by other great seers: / Rudra, Bhṛgu, Marīci, Aṅgiras, Pulaha, Kratu,

1.70.s:
pulastyo 'trir vasiṣṭhaś ca pitaro 'gnistathaiva ca
satīṃ bhavāya prāyacchat khyātiṃ ca bhṛgave tataḥ //
1.70.d:
पुलस्त्यो ऽत्रिर् वसिष्ठश् च पितरो ऽग्निस्तथैव च
सतीं भवाय प्रायच्छत् ख्यातिं च भृगवे ततः ॥
1.70.m: Pulastya, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, the Pitṛs, and Agni. / He gave Satī to Bhava, and then Khyāti to Bhṛgu;

1.70.s:
marīcaye ca saṃbhūtiṃ smṛtimaṅgirase dadau
prītiṃ caiva pulastyāya kṣamāṃ vai pulahāya ca //
1.70.d:
मरीचये च संभूतिं स्मृतिमङ्गिरसे ददौ
प्रीतिं चैव पुलस्त्याय क्षमां वै पुलहाय च ॥
1.70.m: he gave Saṃbhūti to Marīci, and Smṛti to Aṅgiras; / Prīti to Pulastya, and Kṣamā to Pulaha;

1.70.s:
kratave saṃnatiṃ nāma anasūyāṃ tathātraye
ūrjāṃ dadau vasiṣṭhāya svāhāmapyagnaye dadau //
1.70.d:
क्रतवे संनतिं नाम अनसूयां तथात्रये
ऊर्जां ददौ वसिष्ठाय स्वाहामप्यग्नये ददौ ॥
1.70.m: to Kratu he gave the one named Saṃnati, and Anasūyā to Atri; / he gave Ūrjā to Vasiṣṭha, and Svāhā to Agni;

1.70.s:
svadhāṃ caiva pitṛbhyastu tāsvapatyā nibodhata
etāḥ sarvā mahābhāgāḥ prajāsvanusṛtāḥ sthitāḥ //
1.70.d:
स्वधां चैव पितृभ्यस्तु तास्वपत्या निबोधत
एताः सर्वा महाभागाः प्रजास्वनुसृताः स्थिताः ॥
1.70.m: and Svadhā to the Pitṛs. Now learn of their offspring. / All these greatly fortunate women remain attending upon their progeny

1.70.s:
manvantareṣu sarveṣu yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam
śraddhā kāmaṃ vijajñe vai darpo lakṣmīsutaḥ smṛtaḥ //
1.70.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु सर्वेषु यावदाभूतसंप्लवम्
श्रद्धा कामं विजज्ञे वै दर्पो लक्ष्मीसुतः स्मृतः ॥
1.70.m: in all manvantaras until the dissolution of beings. / Śraddhā gave birth to Kāma; Darpa is known as the son of Lakṣmī.

1.70.s:
dhṛtyāstu niyamaḥ putras tuṣṭyāḥ saṃtoṣa eva ca
puṣṭyā lobhaḥ sutaścāpi medhāputraḥ śrutas tathā //
1.70.d:
धृत्यास्तु नियमः पुत्रस् तुष्ट्याः संतोष एव च
पुष्ट्या लोभः सुतश्चापि मेधापुत्रः श्रुतस् तथा ॥
1.70.m: Niyama was the son of Dhṛti, and Saṃtoṣa was the son of Tuṣṭi; / Lobha was the son of Puṣṭi, and Śruta was the son of Medhā.

1.70.s:
kriyāyāmabhavatputro daṇḍaḥ samaya eva ca
buddhyāṃ bodhaḥ sutas tadvat pramādo 'pyupajāyata //
1.70.d:
क्रियायामभवत्पुत्रो दण्डः समय एव च
बुद्ध्यां बोधः सुतस् तद्वत् प्रमादो ऽप्युपजायत ॥
1.70.m: Upon Kriyā were born Daṇḍa and Samaya; / Bodha was born as the son upon Buddhi, and likewise Pramāda was born.

1.70.s:
lajjāyāṃ vinayaḥ putro vyavasāyo vasoḥ sutaḥ
kṣemaḥ śāntisutaścāpi sukhaṃ siddhervyajāyata //
1.70.d:
लज्जायां विनयः पुत्रो व्यवसायो वसोः सुतः
क्षेमः शान्तिसुतश्चापि सुखं सिद्धेर्व्यजायत ॥
1.70.m: Vinaya was the son born of Lajjā; Vyavasāya was the son of Vasu; / Kṣema was the son of Śānti, and Sukha was born of Siddhi.

1.70.s:
yaśaḥ kīrtisutaścāpi ityete dharmasūnavaḥ
kāmasya harṣaḥ putro vai devyāṃ prītyāṃ vyajāyata //
1.70.d:
यशः कीर्तिसुतश्चापि इत्येते धर्मसूनवः
कामस्य हर्षः पुत्रो वै देव्यां प्रीत्यां व्यजायत ॥
1.70.m: Yaśas was the son of Kīrti: these were the sons of Dharma. / Harṣa was born as the son of Kāma upon the goddess Prīti.

1.70.s:
ityeṣa vai sutodarkaḥ sargo dharmasya kīrtitaḥ
jajñe hiṃsā tvadharmādvai nikṛtiṃ cānṛtaṃ sutam //
1.70.d:
इत्येष वै सुतोदर्कः सर्गो धर्मस्य कीर्तितः
जज्ञे हिंसा त्वधर्माद्वै निकृतिं चानृतं सुतम् ॥
1.70.m: Thus the creation of Dharma, bearing this offspring, has been proclaimed. / From Adharma, however, Hiṃsā bore Nikṛti, and the son Anṛta.

1.70.s:
nikṛtyāṃ tu dvayaṃ jajñe bhayaṃ naraka eva ca
māyā ca vedanā cāpi mithunadvayametayoḥ //
1.70.d:
निकृत्यां तु द्वयं जज्ञे भयं नरक एव च
माया च वेदना चापि मिथुनद्वयमेतयोः ॥
1.70.m: From Nikṛti were born a pair: Bhaya and Naraka; / and from these two [came] two couples: Māyā and Vedanā.

1.70.s:
bhūyo jajñe 'tha vai māyā mṛtyuṃ bhūtāpahāriṇam
vedanāyāḥ sutaścāpi duḥkhaṃ jajñe ca rauravaḥ //
1.70.d:
भूयो जज्ञे ऽथ वै माया मृत्युं भूतापहारिणम्
वेदनायाः सुतश्चापि दुःखं जज्ञे च रौरवः ॥
1.70.m: Then Māyā further bore Mṛtyu, the snatcher of creatures; / and as the son of Vedanā Duḥkha was born, and Raurava.

1.70.s:
mṛtyor vyādhijarāśokakrodhāsūyāś ca jajñire
duḥkhottarāḥ sutā hyete sarve cādharmalakṣaṇāḥ //
1.70.d:
मृत्योर् व्याधिजराशोकक्रोधासूयाश् च जज्ञिरे
दुःखोत्तराः सुता ह्येते सर्वे चाधर्मलक्षणाः ॥
1.70.m: From Mṛtyu were born Vyādhi, Jarā, Śoka, Krodha, and Asūyā. / These sons are full of misery, and all have the mark of Adharma.

1.70.s:
naiṣāṃ bhāryāstu putrāś ca sarve hyete parigrahāḥ
ityeṣa tāmasaḥ sargo jajñe dharmaniyāmakaḥ //
1.70.d:
नैषां भार्यास्तु पुत्राश् च सर्वे ह्येते परिग्रहाः
इत्येष तामसः सर्गो जज्ञे धर्मनियामकः ॥
1.70.m: They have neither wives nor sons; for all these are merely belongings. / Thus this creation of darkness was born, acting as the restraint of Dharma.

1.70.s:
prajāḥ sṛjeti vyādiṣṭo brahmaṇā nīlalohitaḥ
so 'bhidhyāya satīṃ bhāryāṃ nirmame hyātmasaṃbhavān //
1.70.d:
प्रजाः सृजेति व्यादिष्टो ब्रह्मणा नीललोहितः
सो ऽभिध्याय सतीं भार्यां निर्ममे ह्यात्मसंभवान् ॥
1.70.m: Commanded by Brahmā, "Create beings," Nīlalohita, / meditating upon his wife Satī, fashioned beings born of himself,

1.70.s:
nādhikānna ca hīnāṃstān mānasānātmanaḥ samān
sahasraṃ hi sahasrāṇāṃ so 'sṛjat kṛttivāsasaḥ //
1.70.d:
नाधिकान्न च हीनांस्तान् मानसानात्मनः समान्
सहस्रं हि सहस्राणां सो ऽसृजत् कृत्तिवाससः ॥
1.70.m: neither superior nor inferior, but mental [beings] equal to himself: / a thousand times thousands he created, clad in animal hides,

1.70.s:
tulyānevātmanaḥ sarvān rūpatejobalaśrutaiḥ
piṅgalānsaniṣaṅgāṃś ca sakapardānsalohitān //
1.70.d:
तुल्यानेवात्मनः सर्वान् रूपतेजोबलश्रुतैः
पिङ्गलान्सनिषङ्गांश् च सकपर्दान्सलोहितान् ॥
1.70.m: all equal to himself in form, splendour, power, and learning, / tawny, carrying quivers, wearing matted hair, reddish,

1.70.s:
viśiṣṭān harikeśāṃś ca dṛṣṭighnāṃś ca kapālinaḥ
mahārūpānvirūpāṃś ca viśvarūpān svarūpiṇaḥ //
1.70.d:
विशिष्टान् हरिकेशांश् च दृष्टिघ्नांश् च कपालिनः
महारूपान्विरूपांश् च विश्वरूपान् स्वरूपिणः ॥
1.70.m: distinguished, with golden-yellow hair, deadly of sight, bearing skulls, / of immense form, misshapen, all-formed, and having their own forms,

1.70.s:
rathinaścarmiṇaścaiva varmiṇaś ca varūthinaḥ
sahasraśatabāhūṃś ca divyān bhaumāntarikṣagān //
1.70.d:
रथिनश्चर्मिणश्चैव वर्मिणश् च वरूथिनः
सहस्रशतबाहूंश् च दिव्यान् भौमान्तरिक्षगान् ॥
1.70.m: charioteers, bearing shields, clad in mail, and with chariot fenders, / with hundreds and thousands of arms, celestial, traversing earth and sky,

1.70.s:
sthūlaśīrṣān aṣṭadaṃṣṭrān dvijihvāṃs tāṃs trilocanān
annādān piśitāśāṃś ca ājyapānsomapānapi //
1.70.d:
स्थूलशीर्षान् अष्टदंष्ट्रान् द्विजिह्वांस् तांस् त्रिलोचनान्
अन्नादान् पिशिताशांश् च आज्यपान्सोमपानपि ॥
1.70.m: thick-headed, with eight fangs, double-tongued, three-eyed, / eating grain and feeding on flesh, drinking clarified butter and drinking soma,

1.70.s:
mīḍhuṣo 'tikapālāṃś ca śitikaṇṭhordhvaretasaḥ
havyādāñchrutadharmāṃś ca dharmiṇo hyatha barhiṇaḥ //
1.70.d:
मीढुषो ऽतिकपालांश् च शितिकण्ठोर्ध्वरेतसः
हव्यादाञ्छ्रुतधर्मांश् च धर्मिणो ह्यथ बर्हिणः ॥
1.70.m: bounteous, carrying great skulls, dark-necked, of upward seed, / consuming sacrificial offerings, conversant with Dharma, righteous, and [dwelling] on sacrificial grass,

1.70.s:
āsīnāndhāvataścaiva pañcabhūtānsahasraśaḥ
adhyāpino 'dhyāyinaś ca japato yuñjatas tathā //
1.70.d:
आसीनान्धावतश्चैव पञ्चभूतान्सहस्रशः
अध्यापिनो ऽध्यायिनश् च जपतो युञ्जतस् तथा ॥
1.70.m: seated and running, composed of the five elements by the thousands, / teachers and students, chanting and practicing yoga,

1.70.s:
dhūmavanto jvalantaś ca nadīmanto 'tidīptinaḥ
vṛddhānbuddhimataścaiva brahmiṣṭhāñśubhadarśanān //
1.70.d:
धूमवन्तो ज्वलन्तश् च नदीमन्तो ऽतिदीप्तिनः
वृद्धान्बुद्धिमतश्चैव ब्रह्मिष्ठाञ्शुभदर्शनान् ॥
1.70.m: smoky, blazing, roaring like rivers, exceedingly luminous, / old, intelligent, deeply devoted to Brahman, and auspicious to behold,

1.70.s:
nīlagrīvān sahasrākṣān sarvāṃścātha kṣamākarān
adṛśyānsarvabhūtānāṃ mahāyogānmahaujasaḥ //
1.70.d:
नीलग्रीवान् सहस्राक्षान् सर्वांश्चाथ क्षमाकरान्
अदृश्यान्सर्वभूतानां महायोगान्महौजसः ॥
1.70.m: blue-throated, thousand-eyed, all showing forbearance, / invisible to all creatures, of great yoga, of great vigour,

1.70.s:
bhramanto 'bhidravantaś ca plavantaś ca sahasraśaḥ
ayātayāmān asṛjad rudrānetān surottamān //
1.70.d:
भ्रमन्तो ऽभिद्रवन्तश् च प्लवन्तश् च सहस्रशः
अयातयामान् असृजद् रुद्रानेतान् सुरोत्तमान् ॥
1.70.m: roaming, charging, and leaping by the thousands: / he created these Rudras, unimpaired, the foremost of gods.

1.70.s:
brahmā dṛṣṭvābravīdenaṃ māsrākṣīrīdṛśīḥ prajāḥ
sraṣṭavyā nātmanastulyāḥ prajā deva namo 'stu te //
1.70.d:
ब्रह्मा दृष्ट्वाब्रवीदेनं मास्राक्षीरीदृशीः प्रजाः
स्रष्टव्या नात्मनस्तुल्याः प्रजा देव नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
1.70.m: Seeing this, Brahmā said to him: "Do not create such creatures! / Creatures equal to oneself must not be created, O god; reverence be to you!

1.70.s:
anyāḥ sṛja tvaṃ bhadraṃ te prajā vai mṛtyusaṃyutāḥ
nārapsyante hi karmāṇi prajāvagatamṛtyavaḥ //
1.70.d:
अन्याः सृज त्वं भद्रं ते प्रजा वै मृत्युसंयुताः
नारप्स्यन्ते हि कर्माणि प्रजावगतमृत्यवः ॥
1.70.m: Create other beings—may you prosper!—beings conjoined with death. / For creatures whose death is absent will never undertake actions."

1.70.s:
evamukto 'bravīdenaṃ nāhaṃ mṛtyujarānvitāḥ
prajāḥ srakṣyāmi bhadraṃ te sthito 'haṃ tvaṃ sṛja prajāḥ //
1.70.d:
एवमुक्तो ऽब्रवीदेनं नाहं मृत्युजरान्विताः
प्रजाः स्रक्ष्यामि भद्रं ते स्थितो ऽहं त्वं सृज प्रजाः ॥
1.70.m: Addressed thus, he said to him: "I will not create creatures / accompanied by death and old age; may you prosper! I shall desist; you create beings.

1.70.s:
ete ye vai mayā sṛṣṭā virūpā nīlalohitāḥ
sahasrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ tu ātmano niḥsṛtāḥ prajāḥ //
1.70.d:
एते ये वै मया सृष्टा विरूपा नीललोहिताः
सहस्राणां सहस्रं तु आत्मनो निःसृताः प्रजाः ॥
1.70.m: These who have been created by me—misshapen, blue and red, / a thousand times thousands, creatures issued from myself—

1.70.s:
ete devā bhaviṣyanti rudrā nāma mahābalāḥ
pṛthivyāmantarikṣe ca dikṣu caiva pariśritāḥ //
1.70.d:
एते देवा भविष्यन्ति रुद्रा नाम महाबलाः
पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे च दिक्षु चैव परिश्रिताः ॥
1.70.m: these shall be gods named Rudras, possessing great power, / residing on the earth, in the intermediate space, and in the directions.

1.70.s:
śatarudrāḥ samātmāno bhaviṣyantīti yājñikāḥ
yajñabhājo bhaviṣyanti sarvadevagaṇaiḥ saha //
1.70.d:
शतरुद्राः समात्मानो भविष्यन्तीति याज्ञिकाः
यज्ञभाजो भविष्यन्ति सर्वदेवगणैः सह ॥
1.70.m: They, of equal nature, shall be known to sacrificers as the hundred Rudras; / they shall be sharers in the sacrifice together with all the hosts of gods.

1.70.s:
manvantareṣu ye devā bhaviṣyantīha bhedataḥ
sārdhaṃ tair ījyamānās te sthāsyantīha ā yugakṣayāt //
1.70.d:
मन्वन्तरेषु ये देवा भविष्यन्तीह भेदतः
सार्धं तैर् ईज्यमानास् ते स्थास्यन्तीह आ युगक्षयात् ॥
1.70.m: Whatever gods there shall be in the various manvantaras here, / being worshipped along with them, they shall remain here until the destruction of the yuga."

1.70.s:
evamuktastadā brahmā mahādevena dhīmatā
pratyuvāca namaskṛtya hṛṣyamāṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ //
1.70.d:
एवमुक्तस्तदा ब्रह्मा महादेवेन धीमता
प्रत्युवाच नमस्कृत्य हृष्यमाणः प्रजापतिः ॥
1.70.m: Addressed thus at that time by wise Mahādeva, / Prajāpati Brahmā bowed and, rejoicing, replied:

1.70.s:
evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te yathā te vyāhṛtaṃ vibho
brahmaṇā samanujñāte tathā sarvamabhūtkila //
1.70.d:
एवं भवतु भद्रं ते यथा ते व्याहृतं विभो
ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञाते तथा सर्वमभूत्किल ॥
1.70.m: “So be it! Blessings upon you, just as you have spoken, O all-pervading lord!” / When Brahmā had given his consent, everything truly became so.

1.70.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti deveśo na cāsūyata vai prajāḥ
ūrdhvaretāḥ sthitaḥ sthāṇur yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam //
1.70.d:
ततः प्रभृति देवेशो न चासूयत वै प्रजाः
ऊर्ध्वरेताः स्थितः स्थाणुर् यावदाभूतसंप्लवम् ॥
1.70.m: From then on, the lord of the gods engendered no offspring at all; / having his semen drawn up, Sthāṇu remained until the cosmic dissolution.

1.70.s:
yasmāduktaḥ sthito 'smīti tasmātsthāṇuriti smṛtaḥ
eṣa devo mahādevaḥ puruṣo 'rkasamadyutiḥ //
1.70.d:
यस्मादुक्तः स्थितो ऽस्मीति तस्मात्स्थाणुरिति स्मृतः
एष देवो महादेवः पुरुषो ऽर्कसमद्युतिः ॥
1.70.m: Because he said, “I remain stationary,” he is therefore remembered as Sthāṇu. / This god is Mahādeva, the Puruṣa radiant as the sun,

1.70.s:
ardhanārīnaravapus tejasā jvalanopamaḥ
svecchayāsau dvidhābhūtaḥ pṛthak strī puruṣaḥ pṛthak //
1.70.d:
अर्धनारीनरवपुस् तेजसा ज्वलनोपमः
स्वेच्छयासौ द्विधाभूतः पृथक् स्त्री पुरुषः पृथक् ॥
1.70.m: having a body half-woman and half-man, blazing like fire in brilliance. / By his own will he became twofold, the woman separate and the man separate.

1.70.s:
sa evaikādaśārdhena sthito 'sau parameśvaraḥ
tatra yā sā mahābhāgā śaṅkarasyārdhakāyinī //
1.70.d:
स एवैकादशार्धेन स्थितो ऽसौ परमेश्वरः
तत्र या सा महाभागा शङ्करस्यार्धकायिनी ॥
1.70.m: That supreme lord remained divided into five and a half parts. / There, she who was the fortunate one, constituting half the body of Śaṅkara,

1.70.s:
prāguktā tu mahādevī strī saiveha satī hyabhūt
hitāya jagatāṃ devī dakṣeṇārādhitā purā //
1.70.d:
प्रागुक्ता तु महादेवी स्त्री सैवेह सती ह्यभूत्
हिताय जगतां देवी दक्षेणाराधिता पुरा ॥
1.70.m: the great goddess previously mentioned—that very woman became Satī here; / for the welfare of the worlds, the goddess had formerly been worshipped by Dakṣa.

1.70.s:
kāryārthaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ tasyāḥ śuklaṃ vāmaṃ tathāsitam
ātmānaṃ vibhajasveti proktā devena śaṃbhunā //
1.70.d:
कार्यार्थं दक्षिणं तस्याः शुक्लं वामं तथासितम्
आत्मानं विभजस्वेति प्रोक्ता देवेन शंभुना ॥
1.70.m: For the purpose of [cosmic] duty, her right side was white and her left was black. / She was told by the lord Śambhu: “Divide yourself!”

1.70.s:
sā tathoktā dvidhābhūtā śuklā kṛṣṇā ca vai dvijāḥ
tasyā nāmāni vakṣyāmi śṛṇvantu ca samāhitāḥ //
1.70.d:
सा तथोक्ता द्विधाभूता शुक्ला कृष्णा च वै द्विजाः
तस्या नामानि वक्ष्यामि शृण्वन्तु च समाहिताः ॥
1.70.m: Addressed thus, she became twofold, white and black, O twice-born ones. / I shall declare her names; listen with concentrated minds:

1.70.s:
svāhā svadhā mahāvidyā medhā lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī
satī dākṣāyaṇī vidyā icchāśaktiḥ kriyātmikā //
1.70.d:
स्वाहा स्वधा महाविद्या मेधा लक्ष्मीः सरस्वती
सती दाक्षायणी विद्या इच्छाशक्तिः क्रियात्मिका ॥
1.70.m: Svāhā, Svadhā, Mahāvidyā, Medhā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, / Satī, Dākṣāyaṇī, Vidyā, the power of will whose nature is action,

1.70.s:
aparṇā caikaparṇā ca tathā caivaikapāṭalā
umā haimavatī caiva kalyāṇī caikamātṛkā //
1.70.d:
अपर्णा चैकपर्णा च तथा चैवैकपाटला
उमा हैमवती चैव कल्याणी चैकमातृका ॥
1.70.m: Aparṇā, Ekaparṇā, and likewise Ekapāṭalā, / Umā, Haimavatī, Kalyāṇī, and Ekamātṛkā,

1.70.s:
khyātiḥ prajñā mahābhāgā loke gaurīti viśrutā
gaṇāṃbikā mahādevī nandinī jātavedasī //
1.70.d:
ख्यातिः प्रज्ञा महाभागा लोके गौरीति विश्रुता
गणांबिका महादेवी नन्दिनी जातवेदसी ॥
1.70.m: Khyāti, Prajñā, the highly fortunate one renowned in the world as Gaurī, / Gaṇāmbikā, Mahādevī, Nandinī, Jātavedasī.

1.70.s:
ekarūpamathaitasyāḥ pṛthagdehavibhāvanāt
sāvitrī varadā puṇyā pāvanī lokaviśrutā //
1.70.d:
एकरूपमथैतस्याः पृथग्देहविभावनात्
सावित्री वरदा पुण्या पावनी लोकविश्रुता ॥
1.70.m: Now, the single form of this goddess, through manifestation in separate bodies, / is Sāvitrī, granter of boons, auspicious, purifying, world-renowned,

1.70.s:
ājñā āveśanī kṛṣṇā tāmasī sāttvikī śivā
prakṛtirvikṛtā raudrī durgā bhadrā pramāthinī //
1.70.d:
आज्ञा आवेशनी कृष्णा तामसी सात्त्विकी शिवा
प्रकृतिर्विकृता रौद्री दुर्गा भद्रा प्रमाथिनी ॥
1.70.m: Ājñā, Āveśanī, Kṛṣṇā, Tāmasī, Sāttvikī, Śivā, / Prakṛti, transformed, Raudrī, Durgā, Bhadrā, Pramāthinī,

1.70.s:
kālarātrirmahāmāyā revatī bhūtanāyikā
dvāparāntavibhāge ca nāmānīmāni suvratāḥ //
1.70.d:
कालरात्रिर्महामाया रेवती भूतनायिका
द्वापरान्तविभागे च नामानीमानि सुव्रताः ॥
1.70.m: Kālarātri, Mahāmāyā, Revatī, Bhūtanāyikā. / And at the junction of the end of the Dvāpara age, these names, O you of noble vows:

1.70.s:
gautamī kauśikī cāryā caṇḍī kātyāyanī satī
kumārī yādavī devī varadā kṛṣṇapiṅgalā //
1.70.d:
गौतमी कौशिकी चार्या चण्डी कात्यायनी सती
कुमारी यादवी देवी वरदा कृष्णपिङ्गला ॥
1.70.m: Gautamī, Kauśikī, Āryā, Caṇḍī, Kātyāyanī, Satī, / Kumārī, Yādavī Devī, granter of boons, Kṛṣṇapiṅgalā,

1.70.s:
barhidhvajā śūladharā paramā brahmacāriṇī
mahendropendrabhaginī dṛṣadvaty ekaśūladhṛk //
1.70.d:
बर्हिध्वजा शूलधरा परमा ब्रह्मचारिणी
महेन्द्रोपेन्द्रभगिनी दृषद्वत्य् एकशूलधृक् ॥
1.70.m: having the peacock-banner, bearer of the trident, supreme, celibate student, / sister of Mahendra and Upendra, Dṛṣadvatī, holder of a single spear,

1.70.s:
aparājitā bahubhujā pragalbhā siṃhavāhinī
śumbhādidaityahantrī ca mahāmahiṣamardinī //
1.70.d:
अपराजिता बहुभुजा प्रगल्भा सिंहवाहिनी
शुम्भादिदैत्यहन्त्री च महामहिषमर्दिनी ॥
1.70.m: unvanquished, many-armed, bold, rider of the lion, / slayer of the daityas such as Śumbha, and crusher of the great Mahiṣa,

1.70.s:
amoghā vindhyanilayā vikrāntā gaṇanāyikā
devyā nāmavikārāṇi ityetāni yathākramam //
1.70.d:
अमोघा विन्ध्यनिलया विक्रान्ता गणनायिका
देव्या नामविकाराणि इत्येतानि यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.70.m: unfailing, dweller on the Vindhya, valiant, leader of the gaṇas. / These are the modifications of the goddess’s names in due order.

1.70.s:
bhadrakālyā mayoktāni samyakphalapradāni ca
ye paṭhanti narāsteṣāṃ vidyate na ca pātakam //
1.70.d:
भद्रकाल्या मयोक्तानि सम्यक्फलप्रदानि च
ये पठन्ति नरास्तेषां विद्यते न च पातकम् ॥
1.70.m: Spoken by me as Bhadrakālī, they bestow complete fruits; / for those men who recite them, no sin exists.

1.70.s:
araṇye parvate vāpi pure vāpyathavā gṛhe
rakṣāmetāṃ prayuñjīta jale vātha sthale 'pi vā //
1.70.d:
अरण्ये पर्वते वापि पुरे वाप्यथवा गृहे
रक्षामेतां प्रयुञ्जीत जले वाथ स्थले ऽपि वा ॥
1.70.m: In a forest or on a mountain, in a city or at home, / in water or on dry land, one should employ this protective spell.

1.70.s:
vyāghrakumbhīnacorebhyo bhayasthāne viśeṣataḥ
āpatsvapi ca sarvāsu devyā nāmāni kīrtayet //
1.70.d:
व्याघ्रकुम्भीनचोरेभ्यो भयस्थाने विशेषतः
आपत्स्वपि च सर्वासु देव्या नामानि कीर्तयेत् ॥
1.70.m: Especially in places of danger from tigers, crocodiles, or thieves, / and in all misfortunes, one should recite the names of the goddess.

1.70.s:
āryakagrahabhūtaiś ca pūtanāmātṛbhis tathā
abhyarditānāṃ bālānāṃ rakṣāmetāṃ prayojayet //
1.70.d:
आर्यकग्रहभूतैश् च पूतनामातृभिस् तथा
अभ्यर्दितानां बालानां रक्षामेतां प्रयोजयेत् ॥
1.70.m: For children afflicted by Āryaka spirits, seizing spirits, and ghosts, / and likewise by Pūtanā and the Mothers, one should apply this protection.

1.70.s:
mahādevīkale dve tu prajñā śrīś ca prakīrtite
ābhyāṃ devīsahasrāṇi yairvyāptamakhilaṃ jagat //
1.70.d:
महादेवीकले द्वे तु प्रज्ञा श्रीश् च प्रकीर्तिते
आभ्यां देवीसहस्राणि यैर्व्याप्तमखिलं जगत् ॥
1.70.m: Prajñā and Śrī are proclaimed as two portions of the great goddess; / by these two [are produced] thousands of goddesses by whom the entire universe is pervaded.

1.70.s:
anayā devadevo 'sau satyā rudro maheśvaraḥ
ātiṣṭhatsarvalokānāṃ hitāya parameśvaraḥ //
1.70.d:
अनया देवदेवो ऽसौ सत्या रुद्रो महेश्वरः
आतिष्ठत्सर्वलोकानां हिताय परमेश्वरः ॥
1.70.m: With this Satī, that god of gods, Rudra Maheśvara, / the supreme lord, remained for the welfare of all the worlds.

1.70.s:
rudraḥ paśupatiścāsīt purā dagdhaṃ puratrayam
devāś ca paśavaḥ sarve babhūvustasya tejasā //
1.70.d:
रुद्रः पशुपतिश्चासीत् पुरा दग्धं पुरत्रयम्
देवाश् च पशवः सर्वे बभूवुस्तस्य तेजसा ॥
1.70.m: Rudra was Paśupati; anciently the triple city was burned, / and all the gods became his beasts by his splendour.

1.70.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi ādisargakramaṃ śubham
sa yāti brahmaṇo lokaṃ śrāvayedvā dvijottamān //
1.70.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद्वापि आदिसर्गक्रमं शुभम्
स याति ब्रह्मणो लोकं श्रावयेद्वा द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
1.70.m: Whoever recites or listens to this auspicious sequence of the primal creation / goes to the realm of Brahmā, or whoever causes the best of the twice-born to hear it.

1.71.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
samāsād vistarāccaiva sargaḥ proktastvayā śubhaḥ
kathaṃ paśupatiścāsīt puraṃ dagdhuṃ maheśvaraḥ //
1.71.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
समासाद् विस्तराच्चैव सर्गः प्रोक्तस्त्वया शुभः
कथं पशुपतिश्चासीत् पुरं दग्धुं महेश्वरः ॥
1.71.m: The sages said: / In brief and in full, the auspicious creation has been recounted by you. / How did Maheśvara become Paśupati in order to burn the city?

1.71.s:
kathaṃ ca paśavaścāsan devāḥ sabrahmakāḥ prabhoḥ
mayasya tapasā pūrvaṃ sudurgaṃ nirmitaṃ puram //
1.71.d:
कथं च पशवश्चासन् देवाः सब्रह्मकाः प्रभोः
मयस्य तपसा पूर्वं सुदुर्गं निर्मितं पुरम् ॥
1.71.m: And how did the gods, along with Brahmā, become the beasts of the lord? / Formerly, by the ascetic power of Maya, an impregnable city was fashioned,

1.71.s:
haimaṃ ca rājataṃ divyam ayasmayam anuttamam
sudurgaṃ devadevena dagdhamityeva naḥ śrutam //
1.71.d:
हैमं च राजतं दिव्यम् अयस्मयम् अनुत्तमम्
सुदुर्गं देवदेवेन दग्धमित्येव नः श्रुतम् ॥
1.71.m: golden, silver, and unsurpassed iron-made, celestial and highly inaccessible; / that it was burned by the god of gods—just this has been heard by us.

1.71.s:
kathaṃ dadāha bhagavān bhaganetranipātanaḥ
ekeneṣunipātena divyenāpi tadā katham //
1.71.d:
कथं ददाह भगवान् भगनेत्रनिपातनः
एकेनेषुनिपातेन दिव्येनापि तदा कथम् ॥
1.71.m: How did the Blessed One, the smiter of Bhaga’s eyes, burn it / then with the release of a single celestial arrow?

1.71.s:
viṣṇunotpāditairbhūtair na dagdhaṃ tatpuratrayam
purasya saṃbhavaḥ sarvo varalābhaḥ purā śrutaḥ //
1.71.d:
विष्णुनोत्पादितैर्भूतैर् न दग्धं तत्पुरत्रयम्
पुरस्य संभवः सर्वो वरलाभः पुरा श्रुतः ॥
1.71.m: That triple city was not burned by the spirits produced by Viṣṇu. / All the origin of the city and the obtaining of the boon was heard previously.

1.71.s:
idānīṃ dahanaṃ sarvaṃ vaktumarhasi suvrata
teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā sūtaḥ paurāṇikottamaḥ //
1.71.d:
इदानीं दहनं सर्वं वक्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सूतः पौराणिकोत्तमः ॥
1.71.m: Now you ought to relate the entire burning, O you of noble vows! / Hearing their statement, Sūta, the best of Purāṇa narrators,

1.71.s:
yathā śrutaṃ tathā prāha vyāsād viśvārthasūcakāt
trailokyasyāsya śāpāddhi manovākkāyasaṃbhavāt //
1.71.d:
यथा श्रुतं तथा प्राह व्यासाद् विश्वार्थसूचकात्
त्रैलोक्यस्यास्य शापाद्धि मनोवाक्कायसंभवात् ॥
1.71.m: spoke just as he had heard from Vyāsa, who reveals the meaning of all things. / Indeed, because of the curse upon the three worlds arising from mind, speech, and body,

1.71.s:
nihate tārake daitye tāraputre sabāndhave
skandena vā prayatnena tasya putrā mahābalāḥ //
1.71.d:
निहते तारके दैत्ये तारपुत्रे सबान्धवे
स्कन्देन वा प्रयत्नेन तस्य पुत्रा महाबलाः ॥
1.71.m: when the daitya Tāraka, the son of Tāra, had been slain along with his kinsmen / by Skanda with strenuous effort, his exceedingly powerful sons—

1.71.s:
vidyunmālī tārakākṣaḥ kamalākṣaś ca vīryavān
tapastepurmahātmāno mahābalaparākramāḥ //
1.71.d:
विद्युन्माली तारकाक्षः कमलाक्षश् च वीर्यवान्
तपस्तेपुर्महात्मानो महाबलपराक्रमाः ॥
1.71.m: Vidyunmālin, Tārakākṣa, and valiant Kamalākṣa, / great-souled ones of immense strength and prowess—performed austerities.

1.71.s:
tapa ugraṃ samāsthāya niyame parame sthitāḥ
tapasā karśayāmāsur dehān svāndānavottamāḥ //
1.71.d:
तप उग्रं समास्थाय नियमे परमे स्थिताः
तपसा कर्शयामासुर् देहान् स्वान्दानवोत्तमाः ॥
1.71.m: Undertaking severe asceticism and abiding by the highest discipline, / those best among dānavas emaciated their bodies through austerities.

1.71.s:
teṣāṃ pitāmahaḥ prīto varadaḥ pradadau varam
avadhyatvaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ sarvabhūteṣu sarvadā //
1.71.d:
तेषां पितामहः प्रीतो वरदः प्रददौ वरम्
अवध्यत्वं च सर्वेषां सर्वभूतेषु सर्वदा ॥
1.71.m: Pleased with them, Pitāmaha, the granter of boons, gave a boon: / invulnerability to all of them among all beings at all times.

1.71.s:
sahitā varayāmāsuḥ sarvalokapitāmaham
tān abravīt tadā devo lokānāṃ prabhur avyayaḥ //
1.71.d:
सहिता वरयामासुः सर्वलोकपितामहम्
तान् अब्रवीत् तदा देवो लोकानां प्रभुर् अव्ययः ॥
1.71.m: Together they chose [this boon] from Pitāmaha of all the worlds. / Then the god, the imperishable lord of the worlds, said to them:

1.71.s:
nāsti sarvāmaratvaṃ vai nivartadhvam ato 'surāḥ
anyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇīdhvaṃ vai yādṛśaṃ samprarocate //
1.71.d:
नास्ति सर्वामरत्वं वै निवर्तध्वम् अतो ऽसुराः
अन्यं वरं वृणीध्वं वै यादृशं सम्प्ररोचते ॥
1.71.m: “Complete immortality does not exist; desist from this, O asuras! / Choose another boon, whatever pleases you well.”

1.71.s:
tataste sahitā daityāḥ sampradhārya parasparam
brahmāṇamabruvandaityāḥ praṇipatya jagadgurum //
1.71.d:
ततस्ते सहिता दैत्याः सम्प्रधार्य परस्परम्
ब्रह्माणमब्रुवन्दैत्याः प्रणिपत्य जगद्गुरुम् ॥
1.71.m: Then those daityas, having deliberated among themselves together, / bowed down to Brahmā, the teacher of the universe, and said:

1.71.s:
vayaṃ purāṇi trīṇyeva samāsthāya mahīmimām
vicariṣyāma lokeśa tvatprasādājjagadguro //
1.71.d:
वयं पुराणि त्रीण्येव समास्थाय महीमिमाम्
विचरिष्याम लोकेश त्वत्प्रसादाज्जगद्गुरो ॥
1.71.m: “Establishing three cities, we shall roam this earth, / O lord of the world, by your grace, O teacher of the universe!”

1.71.s:
tathā varṣasahasreṣu sameṣyāmaḥ parasparam
ekībhāvaṃ gamiṣyanti purāṇyetāni cānagha //
1.71.d:
तथा वर्षसहस्रेषु समेष्यामः परस्परम्
एकीभावं गमिष्यन्ति पुराण्येतानि चानघ ॥
1.71.m: Then, after thousands of years, we shall meet together; / and these cities will merge into unity, O sinless one!

1.71.s:
samāgatāni caitāni yo hanyādbhagavaṃstadā
ekenaiveṣuṇā devaḥ sa no mṛtyurbhaviṣyati //
1.71.d:
समागतानि चैतानि यो हन्याद्भगवंस्तदा
एकेनैवेषुणा देवः स नो मृत्युर्भविष्यति ॥
1.71.m: And when they have come together, O Lord, whoever destroys them then, / [let that] god with a single arrow be our death.

1.71.s:
evamastviti tāndevaḥ pratyuktvā prāviśaddivam
tato mayaḥ svatapasā cakre vīraḥ purāṇyatha //
1.71.d:
एवमस्त्विति तान्देवः प्रत्युक्त्वा प्राविशद्दिवम्
ततो मयः स्वतपसा चक्रे वीरः पुराण्यथ ॥
1.71.m: Having said to them, "So be it," the god entered heaven. / Then the heroic Maya, by his own ascetic heat, fashioned the cities.

1.71.s:
kāñcanaṃ divi tatrāsīd antarikṣe ca rājatam
āyasaṃ cābhavad bhūmau puraṃ teṣāṃ mahātmanām //
1.71.d:
काञ्चनं दिवि तत्रासीद् अन्तरिक्षे च राजतम्
आयसं चाभवद् भूमौ पुरं तेषां महात्मनाम् ॥
1.71.m: The golden one was in heaven, the silver one in the mid-region, / and the iron one was on earth—the cities of those great-souled ones.

1.71.s:
ekaikaṃ yojanaśataṃ vistārāyāmataḥ samam
kāñcanaṃ tārakākṣasya kamalākṣasya rājatam //
1.71.d:
एकैकं योजनशतं विस्तारायामतः समम्
काञ्चनं तारकाक्षस्य कमलाक्षस्य राजतम् ॥
1.71.m: Each one was a hundred yojanas, equal in breadth and length: / the golden one belonged to Tārakākṣa, the silver one to Kamalākṣa,

1.71.s:
vidyunmāleścāyasaṃ vai trividhaṃ durgamuttamam
mayaś ca balavāṃstatra daityadānavapūjitaḥ //
1.71.d:
विद्युन्मालेश्चायसं वै त्रिविधं दुर्गमुत्तमम्
मयश् च बलवांस्तत्र दैत्यदानवपूजितः ॥
1.71.m: and the iron one to Vidyunmālin—three kinds of excellent fortresses. / And the mighty Maya was worshipped there by the Daityas and Dānavas.

1.71.s:
hairaṇye rājate caiva kṛṣṇāyasamaye tathā
ālayaṃ cātmanaḥ kṛtvā tatrāste balavāṃstadā //
1.71.d:
हैरण्ये राजते चैव कृष्णायसमये तथा
आलयं चात्मनः कृत्वा तत्रास्ते बलवांस्तदा ॥
1.71.m: In the golden, the silver, and likewise in the dark-iron [city], / making his own residence, the mighty one dwelt there at that time.

1.71.s:
evaṃ babhūvurdaityānām atidurgāṇi suvratāḥ
purāṇi trīṇi viprendrās trailokyamiva cāparam //
1.71.d:
एवं बभूवुर्दैत्यानाम् अतिदुर्गाणि सुव्रताः
पुराणि त्रीणि विप्रेन्द्रास् त्रैलोक्यमिव चापरम् ॥
1.71.m: Thus the three cities of the Daityas became exceedingly inaccessible, O observers of good vows, / O best of Brahmins, like another triple world.

1.71.s:
puratraye tadā jāte sarve daityā jagattraye
puratrayaṃ praviśyaiva babhūvuste balādhikāḥ //
1.71.d:
पुरत्रये तदा जाते सर्वे दैत्या जगत्त्रये
पुरत्रयं प्रविश्यैव बभूवुस्ते बलाधिकाः ॥
1.71.m: When the triad of cities was produced then, all the Daityas in the three worlds, / having entered that very triad of cities, became superior in strength.

1.71.s:
kalpadrumasamākīrṇaṃ gajavājisamākulam
nānāprasādasaṃkīrṇaṃ maṇijālaiḥ samāvṛtam //
1.71.d:
कल्पद्रुमसमाकीर्णं गजवाजिसमाकुलम्
नानाप्रसादसंकीर्णं मणिजालैः समावृतम् ॥
1.71.m: It was crowded with wish-fulfilling trees, filled with elephants and horses, / crowded with various palaces, covered with nets of gems,

1.71.s:
sūryamaṇḍalasaṃkāśair vimānairviśvatomukhaiḥ
padmarāgamayaiḥ śubhraiḥ śobhitaṃ candrasaṃnibhaiḥ //
1.71.d:
सूर्यमण्डलसंकाशैर् विमानैर्विश्वतोमुखैः
पद्मरागमयैः शुभ्रैः शोभितं चन्द्रसंनिभैः ॥
1.71.m: adorned with aerial chariots facing all directions, resembling the solar disc, / made of rubies, radiant, resembling the moon,

1.71.s:
prāsādairgopurairdivyaiḥ kailāsaśikharopamaiḥ
śobhitaṃ tripuraṃ teṣāṃ pṛthakpṛthaganuttamaiḥ //
1.71.d:
प्रासादैर्गोपुरैर्दिव्यैः कैलासशिखरोपमैः
शोभितं त्रिपुरं तेषां पृथक्पृथगनुत्तमैः ॥
1.71.m: adorned with mansions and divine gateways resembling the peak of Kailāsa, / their Tripura [was adorned], each separately unmatched,

1.71.s:
divyastrībhiḥ susampūrṇaṃ gandharvaiḥ siddhacāraṇaiḥ
rudrālayaiḥ pratigṛhaṃ sāgnihotrair dvijottamāḥ //
1.71.d:
दिव्यस्त्रीभिः सुसम्पूर्णं गन्धर्वैः सिद्धचारणैः
रुद्रालयैः प्रतिगृहं साग्निहोत्रैर् द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
1.71.m: completely filled with divine women, Gandharvas, Siddhas, and Cāraṇas, / with shrines to Rudra in every house, along with Agnihotra fires, O best of the twice-born,

1.71.s:
vāpīkūpataḍāgaiś ca dīrghikābhistu sarvataḥ
mattamātaṅgayūthaiś ca turaṅgaiś ca suśobhanaiḥ //
1.71.d:
वापीकूपतडागैश् च दीर्घिकाभिस्तु सर्वतः
मत्तमातङ्गयूथैश् च तुरङ्गैश् च सुशोभनैः ॥
1.71.m: and with step-wells, deep wells, ponds, and elongated reservoirs on all sides, / with herds of rutting elephants and exceedingly beautiful horses,

1.71.s:
rathaiś ca vividhākārair vicitrairviśvatomukhaiḥ
sabhāprapādibhiś caiva krīḍāsthānaiḥ pṛthak pṛthak //
1.71.d:
रथैश् च विविधाकारैर् विचित्रैर्विश्वतोमुखैः
सभाप्रपादिभिश् चैव क्रीडास्थानैः पृथक् पृथक् ॥
1.71.m: and with chariots of diverse forms, wondrous, facing every direction, / with assembly halls, water-sheds, and separate pleasure-grounds,

1.71.s:
vedādhyayanaśālābhir vividhābhiḥ samantataḥ
adhṛṣyaṃ manasāpyanyair mayasyaiva ca māyayā //
1.71.d:
वेदाध्ययनशालाभिर् विविधाभिः समन्ततः
अधृष्यं मनसाप्यन्यैर् मयस्यैव च मायया ॥
